name: P30

It is the core choice for independent film and television creators who pursue unique texture and retro aesthetics.

name: Eterna 8583/400T
description: Fujifilm Eterna 8583/400T is a professional film negative film, not an ordinary civilian film. It is an ISO 400 photosensitive film designed for use with tungsten light sources and is suitable for indoor or night photography. The film is known for its fine grain, extremely high dynamic range and unique color science. The image contrast is low, the shadow transition is soft, and the skin color appears rosy and natural, which can easily create a story-telling movie lens texture.

name: Eterna Vivid 8543/160T
description:
Fujifilm Eterna Vivid 8543/160T is a professional film negative film. The sensitivity is ISO 160 and has been color temperature balanced with tungsten lamps, making it suitable for indoor lighting photography.
As a member of the Eterna series, it inherits the brand's consistent low grain, high definition and excellent color dynamic range. The low-sensitivity characteristics ensure that the picture is pure and rich in details. “VIVID” indicates that its color performance may be more vivid, taking into account both naturalness and vividness. This is a special film designed for film creators who pursue ultimate image quality and precise tones.

name: Eterna Vivid 8546/250D
description: Fujifilm Eterna Vivid 8546/250D is the professional imaging style of Fujifilm's Eterna series. ISO 250, daylight balanced, suitable for outdoor light. The "Vivid" label emphasizes that its color performance is more vivid, restoring natural skin color while improving color saturation and visual impact. This specification has excellent dynamic range, soft highlights, and complete shadow details. The imaging grains are fine and the texture is warm and moist, taking into account the purity of modern technology and the unique charm of film. This film can produce excellent images with high saturation and low noise, making it an ideal choice for creators who pursue high image quality and vivid tones.

name: Eterna Vivid 8547/500T
description: Fujifilm Eterna Vivid 8547/500T is a roll of classic film-quality color negative film. It has a sensitivity of ISO 500 and is designed for 3200K tungsten lighting. The film is known for its extremely fine grain, excellent color reproduction and wide dynamic range. In terms of color science, it shows a typical "Fuji green" tendency, with soft highlights, deep shadows, and pink and natural skin colors. Because of its unique film texture and scarcity, it is favored by independent photographers and directors, and is often used to create narrative imaging works.

name: F-II
description: Fujicolor F-II is an epoch-making color negative film launched by Fujifilm in the 1970s. It was the first film developed by Fujifilm using the standard C-41 process. F-II is known for its fine grain and extremely natural color reproduction, especially in daylight. Compared with its contemporary competitors, it can present a clearer skin tone and a slightly cooler tone. This unique color tendency later became the origin of Fuji's "green tone" gene. Although this model has long been discontinued, as the pioneer of Fuji's modern color film, it is still regarded as a classic by many old-school photographers. The nostalgic atmosphere and warm tones it brings are difficult to completely replicate with digital simulations.

name: F-Series 8510/64T
description: Fujifilm F-Series 8510/64T is a low-sensitivity light-type film negative (Tungsten Type) in the F series. It is specially designed for indoor artificial light environments, and the low sensitivity of ISO 64 brings extremely delicate tones and pure dark performance. At a color temperature of 3200K, it delivers accurate color reproduction, making it ideal for shooting commercials or movie features that require high definition in studios with strictly controlled lighting.

name: F-Series 8520/64D
description: Fujifilm F-Series 8520/64D is the daylight type roll with the purest image quality among the F-Series. Thanks to its low sensitivity of ISO 64, it has the finest grain performance in the series. In full sunlight, it captures rich detail and wide dynamic range. Its colors tend to be realistic, with greens and blues appearing particularly transparent, making it the first choice for shooting large outdoor scenery and bright locations.

name: F-Series 8530/125T
description: Fujifilm F-Series 8530/125T is a medium-speed light negative film that balances speed and image quality. The ISO 125 setting makes it more flexible when shooting than the F-64T, maintaining excellent sharpness and latitude in slightly darker lighting conditions. It was a workhorse for many mid-budget feature films at the time, handling complex tonal changes well and maintaining smooth transitions of skin tones.

name: F-Series 8550/250T
description: Fujifilm F-Series 8550/250T is a very popular high-sensitivity light-type roll in the F-series. The speed of ISO 250 combined with Fujifilm's grain technology gives it amazing resolution in low light. It performs stably when processing mixed light sources (Mixed Lighting), with rich dark details and no distortion. It is the core strength of shooting indoor scenes at night and low-light scenes.

name: F-Series 8560/250D
description: The Fujifilm F-Series 8560/250D is a high-speed daylight film reel. It is specially designed for outdoor environments with slightly lower illumination such as cloudy days, dusk or shaded areas. A sensitivity of ISO 250 allows photographers to achieve sufficient depth of field without sacrificing shutter speed. It inherits the consistent warm tone of Fujifilm, with bright but not exaggerated colors, and excellent post-production color grading space.

name: F-Series 8570/500T
description: Fujifilm F-Series 8570/500T is the most powerful high-sensitivity light reel in the F-Series. As a "speed monster" with ISO 500, it is designed for extremely dark environments or artistic creations that pursue grainy textures. Even at high sensitivities, it maintains good contrast control and color saturation. It was the first choice for many dark-style movies or documentaries in the 1990s, capturing faint light and shadows that are difficult to detect with the naked eye.

name: Fujichrome 100
description: Fujichrome 100 is Fujifilm's most classic early general-purpose professional color reversal film and the predecessor of the later famous Provia 100. Known for its fine grain (RMS 8) and neutral-to-cool tones, this film is capable of producing very pure whites and deep blacks. It has unparalleled transparency when expressing metal textures, glass and landscapes under early morning sunlight. An all-rounder, it was the industry standard for commercial and product photography.

name: Fujichrome 100D
description: Fujichrome 100D is a model that further improves sharpness and color saturation based on 100. Its "D" stands for Daylight Balance, designed to capture the real world at a standard color temperature of 5500K. It has a very high degree of separation of the three primary colors of red, green and blue, and the imaging colors are bright but not overly exaggerated, and it has a very high tolerance (within the scope of reversal film). It was the go-to choice for landscape photographers in the 1990s in well-lit situations, with mirror-smooth image quality.

name: Fujichrome 400D
description: Fujichrome 400D is a high-performance, high-sensitivity daylight reversal film. In the field of reversal film, it is very difficult to maintain high sensitivity while maintaining delicate image quality, but the 400D does it. It not only has excellent color vividness, but also maintains excellent details in low light or high-speed shutter shooting. It is often used for sports photography, wildlife capture, and fashion outdoor photography with changing light. It is the ultimate tool for photographers who pursue a balance between speed and image quality.

name: Fujichrome 50D
description: Fujichrome 50D is the “enthusiast” choice for ultimate resolution and saturation. As a low-sensitivity ISO 50 film, its graininess is almost invisible, and its images are extremely high-contrast and rich in color. It is very sensitive to light and can produce stunning transparency and three-dimensionality under sufficient side backlighting. It is the favorite for shooting large-format landscapes and high-precision still life photography. Every negative is like a beautiful work of art.

name: Fujichrome P1600D
description: Fujichrome P1600D is the "child of the night" in Fujifilm's reversal film family. It is an ultra-high-sensitivity daylight reversal film specially designed to achieve ISO 1600 through push processing. Although the grain is coarse, it has a very unique and dramatic high-contrast effect. It can still capture vivid colors in extremely dark environments, making it ideal for shooting concerts, night documentaries, or special occasions that require extremely fast shutter speeds, opening up the possibility of reverse film photography in the dark.

name: HR 100
description: Fujicolor HR100 is a high-performance color negative film launched by Fujifilm in the 1980s. The “HR” in its name stands for “High Resolution”. As Fujifilm's main product at the time, the HR100 introduced revolutionary dual-structure photosensitive particle technology, which significantly improved the sharpness and detail expression of the picture. This film is admired for its extremely fine grain, wide exposure latitude, and quintessential "Fuji tone" - crisp green and blue reproduction. Whether in bright outdoor sunlight or complex diffuse light environments, the HR100 delivers extremely stable and natural tones. It was the model that helped Fujifilm enter the global modern imaging market, and also laid the technical foundation for the Superia series that later became a household name.

name: HR 200
description: Fujicolor HR 200 is a color negative film launched by Fujifilm in the 1980s that combines high image quality with practicality. As the backbone of the HR (High Resolution) series, it perfectly balances photosensitivity speed and image detail. HR 200 adopted the then-advanced "dual structure grain" technology, which allowed it to have a higher sensitivity than traditional film while still maintaining stunning sharpness and minimal graininess. Its color performance inherits Fuji's consistent natural freshness, with a warm restoration of reds and yellows, and appears particularly transparent when dealing with green vegetation and blue skies. Due to its excellent exposure latitude, it became the first choice for many family travel photographers and amateurs at that time. Whether it was outdoor shooting on a sunny day or indoor shooting with flash, it could provide stable and reliable image quality.

name: Industrial 100
description: Fujifilm Business 100 is a color negative film launched by Fujifilm for commercial use. The ISO 100 sensitivity ensures excellent detail performance and color saturation. This film is specially designed for professional photographers and commercial photography scenes, providing accurate color reproduction and excellent exposure latitude. Business 100 performs well in studio shooting, product photography, portrait photography and other fields, delivering clear and sharp images and natural skin tones. Its fine grain structure and good scanning performance make it an ideal choice for those pursuing high-quality commercial images.

name: Industrial 400
description: Fujifilm Business 400 is a nominally ISO400 color negative film originally marketed as Fujifilm's "Business/Industrial Recording Film" for use in both documentary photography and general use. The imaging style of Fujifilm Business Volume 400 is famous for its natural colors, low contrast, and soft tones, and has been evaluated by many users as a "healing" style: Compared with traditional consumer-grade color films, it is more sensitive to warm light sources, has slightly lower overall contrast, and softer and more delicate colors. The captured images often have a soothing and warm atmosphere, which is especially suitable for portraits, daily street photography, and natural light scenes.

name: Instax Square Instant Film
description: The Fujifilm Instax Square series uses a square format of 62×62mm and an effective image area of ​​approximately 54×54mm, making it an ideal choice for pursuing creative compositions and symmetrical beauty. SQ series films have bright and full color performance and fine grains, making them suitable for portraits, creative poses, and artistic photography. The square format allows for more freedom in composition and more visual impact in social sharing and handcrafting. The development time is about 90 seconds, and the imaging is fast and stable.

name: Instax Wide Instant Film
description: Fujifilm Instax Wide is the largest format film among Fujifilm instant films, with a size of approximately 86×108mm (image effective area of ​​approximately 62×99mm), and is suitable for Wide series cameras. Large-format film can provide a wider viewing space and delicate gradation expression, which is very suitable for group portraits, landscapes, indoor scenes or creations that require large backgrounds. Wide film has bright and natural colors, fine grains, good exposure latitude, stable imaging, and can better demonstrate the sense of space and depth of field.

name: Instax mini Instant Film
description: Fujifilm Instax Mini is Fujifilm’s most classic instant format, with a frame size of approximately 54×86mm (image effective area of ​​approximately 46×62mm). This film is a color instant imaging film that supports direct camera exposure and automatic development, and can be imaged in about 90 seconds after the shooting is completed. Mini film has bright colors, good exposure latitude, and fine grain, making it suitable for easy creation of portraits, parties, travel records, etc. Its compact format makes it easy to collect or create instant photo albums, and is very popular among students and young photography enthusiasts.

name: Jelly
description: Fujifilm Jelly is a fun disposable camera launched by Fujifilm for trendy gamers and fashion groups. As one of the most beautiful designs in the QuickSnap family, its most notable feature is its brightly colored, translucent jelly-colored shell, which gives people a crystal-clear visual enjoyment like candy. In terms of imaging, Jelly uses Fujifilm's high-standard ISO 400 color negative film, which has natural color reproduction, moderate saturation, and excellent transparency when expressing skin colors and outdoor natural light. Its ultra-light body and built-in sliding flash make shooting easy and fun, making it ideal for taking with you at gatherings, parties, or on energetic trips. Jelly is not only a reliable film camera for recording beautiful moments, but also a highly recognizable fashion accessory for photography enthusiasts.

name: MS 100/1000
description: Fujichrome MS 100/1000 is one of the most powerful and versatile professional models in Fujifilm's reversal film family. The core design concept of this film is "multi-sensitivity adaptability". Its nominal sensitivity is ISO 100, but through professional push processing, its sensitivity can be smoothly increased to ISO 1000 or even higher, while still maintaining excellent color balance and contrast control. The MS 100/1000 uses Fujifilm's unique Sigma grain technology, which allows the grains to remain compact and sharp when forced to process to high sensitivities, without the severe color cast or gray background common with ordinary reversal films. It is the first choice for sports photographers, war reporters and extreme adventurers, providing professional-level image protection in extreme environments ranging from bright sunlight to weak moonlight.

name: Natura 1600 NP
description:
Natura 1600 NP is a high-sensitivity color negative film with a sensitivity of ISO 1600. It has been widely used in street photography and documentary photography in low-light environments.
The most notable feature of this film is the iconic "Fuji Green" tone, which is cold in color, high in contrast, and has an obvious graininess, creating a retro and emotionally charged atmosphere. Compared with similar products, its color style is more personalized and suitable for expressing specific themes.

name: Neopan 400
description:
Neopan 400 is a high-performance black and white negative film with an ISO 400 sensitivity making it suitable for all-weather shooting. It performs well in low light, with fine particles, rich image levels, and natural grayscale transitions.
Compared with similar high-speed films, it has higher exposure latitude and high error tolerance, making it suitable for novices and documentary photography. It needs to be washed with conventional black and white developer, which can restore deep black and rich mid-tones, inheriting the traditional texture and ensuring stable quality. Whether it is street photography or humanistic creation, it can give the picture a unique narrative and emotional tension, making it an excellent choice to experience the charm of film.

name: Oxygen
description: Fujifilm Oxygen is a high-looking special edition disposable camera launched by Fujifilm for the young market. As a derivative of the classic QuickSnap series, Oxygen is most eye-catching for its translucent cyan blue shell design, which is full of refreshing "airy" and modern industrial design aesthetics. The camera has built-in Fuji high-quality color negative film at ISO 200. The imaging style continues Fuji's classic cool tones, with particularly outstanding performance on greens and blues. The colors are transparent and have a Japanese lightness. Its compact and lightweight body combined with simple one-touch flash operation makes it an ideal choice for beach vacations, summer picnics or street photography. It is not only a recording tool with stable performance, but also a fashionable item with great personality.

name: Pro 160C
description: Fujifilm Pro 160C is Fujifilm's professional-grade color negative film. The medium and low speed sensitivity of ISO 160 provides excellent image quality performance. The film is known for its cool color bias, producing crisp, transparent blues and greens. The Pro 160c has fine grain and moderate color saturation, making it particularly suitable for landscape, portrait and commercial photography. Although it has been discontinued, its unique color style and excellent image quality are still missed by many photographers. In the market, Pro 160c stock film has become a collectible, representing Fujifilm's classic tradition and professional standards.

name: Pro 160NS
description: Fujifilm Pro 160NS is Fujifilm's professional-grade color negative film, and "NS" stands for Natural Skin. The ISO 160 sensitivity provides delicate picture quality and good color reproduction. Compared with the Pro 160c, the 160NS has a warmer and more neutral color tone, which is particularly suitable for portrait photography and can perfectly present natural skin tone transitions. This film has fine grain and excellent latitude, making it popular in professional portrait and wedding photography. Although it has been discontinued, Pro 160NS is still regarded as a classic of Fujifilm portrait film, and the elegant colors it displays are unforgettable.

name: Pro 400H
description: Fujifilm Pro 400H is Fujifilm’s most famous professional-grade portrait film and is known as the “King of Fujifilm Portraits”. The ISO 400 sensitivity provides good adaptability and is suitable for a variety of light environments. Known for its crystal clear colors, ultra-low contrast and soft highlight transitions, the Pro 400H is particularly suitable for portraits, weddings and fashion photography. The film's extremely fine grain produces a unique "Fuji green" hue and airy feel. Unfortunately, the Pro 400H has been discontinued in 2021 and has become a classic legend in the history of film photography. Its market price soared, making it a film prized by collectors and photographers.

name: Provia 100
description: Provia 100 (RDP) is the foundation of Fujifilm's professional reversal film system. A professional standard in the late 1980s and early 1990s, it was known for its extremely balanced color reproduction and excellent skin tone representation. Unlike the later 100F, which pursued absolute neutrality, the original Provia 100 had a warmer tone, with a faint cyan-blue tint in the shadows. This "Fuji Blue" became the signature of many fashion photographers at the time. It was the universal first choice for pictorial photography, outdoor portraits and all kinds of professional records of that era.

name: Provia 100F
description: Fujifilm Provia 100F is Fujifilm's professional-grade slide film, and the "F" stands for Fine. Made as ISO 100 daylight positive film, using E-6 processing process. Known for its neutral and accurate color reproduction, fine grain and excellent sharpness, the Provia 100F is ideal for landscape and commercial photography. This film has moderate color saturation and mild contrast, giving it a true and natural look. Compared with the Velvia series, the color of Provia 100F is more neutral and objective, suitable for professional work that requires accurate color reproduction. The Provia 100F is the most balanced and versatile choice among Fujifilm slides.

name: Provia 1600
description: Provia 1600 (RSP) is a professional tool developed by Fujifilm specifically to challenge the limits of low light. It is actually a film optimized for push processing and is officially recommended for use at ISO 1600 or higher. Its tone style is very tough and the contrast is strong, and it can produce images with great grain tension and visual impact. It is a special tool in stage photography, late-night documentary and military/scientific observation, preserving the last creative possibilities for photographers in almost no light environments.

name: Provia 400
description: Provia 400 (RHP) is a high-speed reversal film that breaks the stereotype of "high sensitivity means high grain". In that era of technological iteration, it delivered very solid color saturation and clarity at a sensitivity of ISO 400. Its contrast distribution is very natural, and it does not easily produce a serious sense of accumulation in the dark areas like ordinary high-sensitivity rolls. It was a favorite of news documentary photographers and sports photographers at that time, especially in the early morning or evening when a slightly faster shutter speed was needed, and it could capture the scene atmosphere full of texture.

name: Provia 400F
description: Provia 400F is a high-performance professional high-sensitivity reversal film launched by Fujifilm around 2000. It is a comprehensive innovation of early RHP technology. By introducing "multi-layer core shell grain" technology, 400F achieves a grain fineness (RMS 13) at a sensitivity of ISO 400 that is almost comparable to that of early ISO 100 films. Its color reproduction is very neutral and accurate, with moderate contrast, making it ideal for capturing natural skin tones and environmental details in complex lighting. More importantly, it has an extremely powerful burst capability, and when forced to ISO 800 or 1600, color cast control remains surprisingly stable.

name: Provia 400X
description: Provia 400X is the ultimate pinnacle of Fujifilm reversal film technology and the swan song in the history of high-sensitivity reversal film. As the successor of 400F, it introduces the "fourth photosensitive layer" technology and new couplers originally used only in film rolls, which greatly improves the saturation of colors and the transparency of the picture while maintaining extremely fine particles. The tone of 400X is slightly more lively than that of 400F, and the colors are more vivid. Especially when expressing the low light of early morning and dusk, it can present a deep and tense tone. It is a dream film for professional outdoor photographers and humanistic photographers. It can still provide pure image quality and charming colors like a low-sensitivity film in dim light moments.

name: Quicksnap
description: Fujifilm Quicksnap is Fujifilm's most famous ready-to-use (disposable) camera with built-in high-sensitivity Fujifilm Quicksnap 400 film, making it the perfect companion for street photography, party and travel documentation. It is equipped with a fixed shutter speed and aperture, as well as an amazing plastic aspherical lens, which can take high-sharp photos with a very "film feel". Its most notable feature is its signature Fuji Green shade, which is colorful and performs well in low light. Whether it's a beach under the scorching sun or an indoor party at night with its built-in flash, Quicksnap can provide stable and retro-ambient imaging effects, making it the first choice tool for many people looking for "pure photography happiness."

name: Quicksnap Fujifilm 400
description: This is a disposable camera with built-in high-sensitivity Fujifilm Quicksnap 400 film, and while many people love the "pure joy of photography" of disposable film cameras, there are also those who will separate the film from the disposable camera to get better imaging results.

name: Reala 8592/500D
description: Fujifilm Reala 8592/500D is a legendary high-speed daylight film negative film. Its biggest feature is the introduction of Fujifilm’s proud “fourth photosensitive layer” technology, which not only gives it an extremely fine graininess (even at a high speed of ISO 500), but also gives it excellent color reproduction capabilities, especially when dealing with color cast problems under complex light sources such as fluorescent lamps. Reala 500D has a strong film-like latitude and extremely soft skin tone performance. The color tends to be natural turquoise, with a signature cold-toned texture in the shadows. Although the film has been discontinued, it is still sought after by many film enthusiasts in the form of "packaging rolls" and is known as one of the most "airy" film films.

name: Sensia 100
description: Fujifilm Sensia 100 is one of Fujifilm's most popular consumer-grade color reversal films. It is known for its extremely fine particles and highly realistic color reproduction. Sensia 100 has a very neutral color tendency, which is not as exaggerated as Velvia. This allows it to show extremely natural and healthy skin tones when shooting portraits, and when shooting landscapes, it can restore the pure sky blue and emerald green that are closest to what the naked eye can see. Since it has a sensitivity of ISO 100, it's best suited for use outdoors in good light, making it a great choice for getting started with slide photography.

name: Sensia 200
description: Fujifilm Sensia 200 is a color reversal film that strikes the perfect balance between sensitivity and image quality. Compared to 100 degrees, its extra sensitivity makes it more adaptable in cloudy weather or at dusk. Although the sensitivity has been increased, it still maintains very smooth tonal transitions and fine graininess. Sensia 200 has moderate contrast and good shadow detail retention, making it ideal for daily recording and travel photography that require both speed and image quality. It's a staple in many film travelers' camera bags because it can handle a wider range of light and shadow changes from early morning to sunset.

name: Sensia 400
description: Fujifilm Sensia 400 is the high-speed model in this series and a rare high-speed multi-function player in the reversal film family. The high sensitivity of ISO 400 makes it easy to shoot in low-light environments, indoors or capture high-speed moving objects. Although as a high-speed film, its graininess is slightly more obvious than that of 100 degrees, Fujifilm's advanced emulsion technology still ensures the transparency of the picture and the accuracy of colors. The Sensia 400 captures highly immersive moments, especially in documentary photography and sports. It is a rare tool for photographers who want to experience the ultimate transparency of reversal film in non-ideal lighting.

name: Sensia II 100
description: The Fujifilm Sensia II 100 is Fujifilm's major upgrade to the first generation Sensia. This film significantly improves color saturation and picture clarity while maintaining the fine graininess of ISO 100. Thanks to the "multi-layer emulsion technology" developed by Fujifilm at the time, Sensia II has more vivid color performance than its predecessor and is more resistant to fading. Its tone transition is very smooth, especially when expressing bright sunlight and clear blue tones, it can present a very transparent visual effect. As a reversal film aimed at ordinary consumers, Sensia II became a long-term "hanging film" for slide photography enthusiasts at the end of the 20th century due to its extremely high cost performance and imaging quality close to the professional film Provia.

name: Super 100
description: Fujifilm Super 100 is a landmark low-sensitivity color negative film launched by Fujifilm. As the base model of Fujifilm's Super series, it's known for its extremely fine grain and stunning sharpness. This film performs particularly well in full daylight, capturing fine textures with precision. Super 100 continues Fujifilm’s signature trend of cool tones, which is especially transparent when dealing with greens and blues, giving a refreshing and natural visual experience. Although it has been gradually replaced by the Superia series and faded out of the market, its robust latitude and age-like color balance make it still a classic "base color" that many film lovers miss.

name: Super 400
description: Fujifilm Super 400 is a high-performance color negative film launched by Fujifilm in the 1990s, designed to provide users with a stable shooting experience in various lighting conditions. The ISO 400 sensitivity gives it great versatility, whether it's indoor low light, dusk or high-speed sports capture. This film applied Fujifilm's "Sigma Fine Grain Technology" at the time, which allowed it to maintain a high sensitivity while still having a fine graininess close to that of ISO 100 film. The Super 400 is known for its natural, vivid color reproduction and excellent skin tone representation, with overall bright tones and Fujifilm's signature crisp green-shade tendencies. As the direct predecessor of the Superia series, it established Fujifilm's leading position in the global market for consumer high-speed negative film.

name: Super F-Series 8522/64D
description: Fujifilm Super F-Series 8522/64D is an ultra-fine grain daylight (5500K) film negative film. As the lowest-sensitivity member of the F series, it represented the pinnacle of Fujifilm image quality at the time. This film has stunning sharpness and almost invisible grain, delivering deep blacks and extremely rich tonal gradations in full sunlight. It is very suitable for shooting large scenes of scenery and materials that require a lot of special effects synthesis in post-production. Due to its extremely fine texture, F-64D is known as one of the most "large-format-looking" 35mm film films.

name: Super F-Series 8532/125T
description: Fujifilm Super F-Series 8532/125T is a medium-speed light-type (3200K) film negative film. Designed specifically for controlled studio lighting environments, it has well-balanced contrast and natural color saturation. The F-125T achieves an extremely delicate balance in skin color reproduction, able to capture the subtlest changes in skin tones without looking harsh. It was the first choice for shooting many TV series and indoor movie scenes at that time, not only because of its excellent image quality, but also because of its extremely high stability from batch to batch.

name: Super F-Series 8552/250T
description: Fujifilm Super F-Series 8552/250D is an all-around daylight balanced film negative. It strikes the perfect balance between speed and image quality, making it one of the most versatile films in the F series. A sensitivity of ISO 250 makes it capable of handling a variety of conditions, from overcast skies to bright outdoors. Its colors tend to be bright and have Fuji's signature refreshing feel, especially when expressing green vegetation and blue skies, with unique artistic appeal. The F-250D is widely used in commercial advertising and location movie shooting, and is a favorite among photographers who pursue natural light quality.

name: Super F-Series 8562/250D
description: Fujifilm Super F-Series 8562/250T is a high-speed light-based film negative designed to give photographers greater aperture choices and deeper depth-of-field control. As a light film, it can provide extremely accurate white balance restoration under tungsten lamps, avoiding the tedious color correction in later stages. The F-250T is known for its smooth shadow transitions and low grain noise, retaining rich details even in slightly darker studio corners. It is the leader in shadow processing in the F series and is often used to create dramatic interior light and shadow atmospheres.

name: Super F-Series 8572/500T
description: The Fujifilm Super F-Series 8572/500T is the high-speed flagship of the series, designed specifically for extremely low-light environments. As an ISO 500 light-type negative film, it adopted Fujifilm's most advanced grain control technology at the time, which not only ensured high sensitivity, but also effectively suppressed the common color noise in high-sensitivity movies. The images it delivers are extremely cinematic, with deep colors and soft skin tones. Whether shooting city night scenes, dark-toned interior dramas, or documentary films pursuing a realistic style, the F-500T delivers convincing visual depth.

name: Super F-Series 8582/400T
description: Fujifilm Super F-Series 8582/400T is a very unique film film that is positioned between the F-250T and F-500T. Fujifilm's original intention in designing this film was to provide a high sensitivity close to 500 degrees while having a detailed image quality closer to that of a medium-speed film. The F-400T is known for its extremely high dynamic range and latitude, able to recover amazing details in both overexposed and underexposed situations. Its color performance is slightly more subtle than that of the 500T, with an elegant gray tone, making it a secret weapon for directors and photographers who pursue a delicate narrative style.

name: Super G 100
description: Fujicolor Super G 100 is Fujifilm's flagship high-quality color negative film launched in the early 1990s. As a direct descendant of the Super HG series, it further strengthens Fujifilm’s proud grain control technology, achieving extremely high resolution and smooth images with almost no graininess at a low sensitivity of ISO 100. The color style of Super G 100 is famous for its bright and bright color style. It shows great vitality in warm tones such as red and orange, while retaining Fujifilm’s signature refreshing green tones. Due to its excellent contrast performance and excellent imaging sharpness, it was not only popular among home users at the time, but was also often used by photography enthusiasts to shoot landscapes and exquisite outdoor portraits. It was synonymous with "high image quality" in the film market in the early 1990s.

name: Super G ACE 400
description: Super G Ace 400 is Fujifilm’s “ace” color negative film launched in the 1990s for high-speed capture and complex light and shadow environments. Compared with the ordinary Super G series, the Ace version has made significant improvements in grain control and color reproduction accuracy. It introduces more advanced coupler technology that can effectively suppress color cast problems (such as common green shades) that easily occur under fluorescent lamps or indoor mixed light sources. The high sensitivity of ISO 400 and the extremely wide exposure latitude make it not only capable of capturing dimly lit indoors, but also maintaining soft contrast and delicate skin tones under strong light. It was once the first choice for many users of high-end zoom point & shoot cameras. Its excellent stability ensures that even under imperfect metering conditions, photos with bright colors and rich details can still be printed.

name: Super G Plus 200
description: Super G Plus 200 is a high-performance color negative film positioned for all-purpose home use. It is the product of a comprehensive optimization of the color algorithm of the previous generation product, especially strengthening the ability to capture warm tones under natural light. The ISO 200 sensitivity gives it great flexibility, allowing it to maintain detailed image quality outdoors in full sunlight, as well as take bright, vivid photos with flash in cloudy weather or indoor environments. It is most praised for its "vividness" of color, which can give ordinary daily records a transparent and slightly cinematic texture. It was the most common source of images in travel photography and family albums in the mid-to-late 1990s.

name: Super G Plus 400
description: Super G Plus 400 is an important technological leap for Fujifilm in the field of high-speed film. It not only inherits the fine-grained characteristics of the Super G series, but also significantly improves the contrast and color purity of the picture. The design of this film focuses on "capture performance" to ensure that details in shadow areas are not lost even at high shutter speeds. Its color performance is more impactful than the 200-degree version, especially the reproduction of reds and greens is very full, making it ideal for street documentaries, sports activities, and indoor captures where the lighting conditions are not ideal. It was a stepping stone for many amateurs at that time to advance to professional image quality, and defined the upper limit of quality for high-sensitivity civilian rolls in the late 1990s.

name: Super HG 100
description: Super HG 100 is a professional/high-end consumer color negative film known for its high definition and color accuracy. Thanks to the new Sigma crystal, its grain performance is tighter and more uniform than the previous generation Super HR, almost eliminating the sense of impurities in the picture. This film is very delicate in the transition of light and shadow, able to capture the smallest changes in texture. Its color tends to be a clear and thorough style, and its performance is particularly outstanding in cool colors (such as sky blue, lake green). It was the first choice for outdoor shooting in the early 1990s by many photographers who pursued commercial-level image quality, and its imaging effects look modern even today.

name: Super HG 400
description: Super HG 400 completely changed people's prejudice against high-speed photosensitive film as "low quality". It was one of the finest-grained ISO 400 color negative films in the world at the time, and Fujifilm succeeded in achieving a breakthrough balance between high sensitivity and high image quality by optimizing the structure of the photosensitive layer. It has slightly livelier tones than the 100-degree version, with moderate contrast and excellent shadow detail retention. Whether in fast-paced street photography or in limited-light indoor environments, the Super HG 400 delivers images with saturated colors and low noise. It was the "workhorse roll" for journalists and enthusiasts in the 1990s and defined the quality benchmark for high-speed negative film of the era.

name: Super HR 100
description: The Super HR 100 is the benchmark in the range for ultimate sharpness and color purity. As a low-sensitivity professional/semi-professional grade negative film, it delivers an amazing level of detail in sufficient light. Compared with the previous generation HR 100, the Super HR 100 is more vivid in red and blue reproduction, and the tones are tighter. It is ideal for shooting static landscapes, detailed architecture, and photography that requires large-format enlargement. Its fine graininess almost represented the highest level of craftsmanship in color negative films at the time.

name: Super HR 1600
description: Super HR 1600 was a technological marvel in Fujifilm’s industrial history and one of the highest-sensitivity color negative films in the world at the time. Designed to challenge the limits of optics, this “child of the night” can shoot without a flash in extremely dark environments, such as theater interiors, night streets or sports venues. Although it has a distinct graininess, this texture is regarded by many photographers as a unique artistic expression. While maintaining a high sensitivity, it can still maintain basic color saturation, leaving precious color images for those moments that would otherwise be impossible to image.

name: Super HR 200
description: The Super HR 200 is a classic model billed as “all-weather wear”. It is designed to provide users with greater flexibility than 100 degrees while maintaining image quality close to that of low-sensitivity film. Thanks to the improved photosensitive emulsion of the Super HR series, it can still maintain a stable color balance without obvious color shift in environments with changing light such as cloudy days or dusk. Its warm skin tone expression and moderate contrast made it an "all-around pocket roll" for travel photographers and family documentarians of the era.

name: Super HR 400
description: Super HR 400 marks the entry into the “practical” era of high-speed negative film. Before its appearance, 400-degree film was often criticized by professional photographers for being too large in grain, but Super HR 400 relies on new grain technology to greatly suppress noise grains while ensuring photosensitive speed. Its ability to capture details in low-light environments is excellent, and it's particularly good at capturing dynamic moments or shooting in indoor environments. Its color tends to be slightly lively, which can inject more vitality into shadow areas. It is the best choice for documentary, snapshot and news photography.

name: Super V  100
description: Super V 100 is Fujifilm’s “pentathlon” of advanced color negative films launched in the early 1990s and is the pinnacle of the Super HG series. The core technology of this film lies in the fine-tuning of the layers of photosensitive emulsion, allowing it to achieve an unprecedented level of "depth" in color. Compared with the previous generation, Super V can present deeper and richer tones, especially in the purity of the three primary colors of red, green and blue. It not only retains the ultra-fine graininess brought by Sigma crystal technology, but also greatly enhances the three-dimensional and airy feel of the picture by improving the coupler. As the most high-end civilian/semi-professional negative film on the market at the time, Super V was widely used in demanding travel photography and portrait creation. Its color style full of thick texture in the 1990s is still the visual standard that many veteran film players miss.

name: Superia 100
description: Superia 100 is the benchmark for daylight negative film that pursues extremely detailed image quality. The lowest-sensitivity member of the series, it boasts extremely fine grain and stunning sharpness. Thanks to the fourth photosensitive layer technology, its color performance under sunlight is extremely transparent, especially the representation of the sky and vegetation with an iconic and elegant "Fuji green". It is ideal for shooting outdoor scenery and exquisite portraits. Even today, it is still regarded by many photographers as the smoothest civilian roll among color negative films and the closest to the texture of reversal film.

name: Superia 1600
description: Superia 1600 is the "king of the night" in the field of consumer color negative film. Before the popularization of high-sensitivity technology in digital cameras, it was one of the very few ultra-high-sensitivity films that could maintain excellent color saturation under weak light. Although its graininess is more obvious, this kind of grain has a strong film texture and grain tension, which can add a deep atmosphere to the photo. It's perfect for capturing indoor concerts, nighttime celebrations or sports events. Due to its unique technical construction, it captures color details far beyond ordinary film in extreme low light, making it an essential tool for exploring the limits of darkness in film photography.

name: Superia 200
description: Superia 200 is the "master of balance" in the Fujifilm family. It's designed to provide a more flexible range than a 100-degree roll without sacrificing too much image quality. This film is known for its extremely high latitude and warm color performance, and can easily handle various light and shadow changes from sunny to cloudy. Its skin color reproduction is very natural and has a touch of Japanese freshness, making it one of the world's best-selling travel and life recording films. It is the first roll of film for many entry-level photographers, and it is also the most reliable and cost-effective daily roll in the eyes of experienced photographers.

name: Superia 400
description: Superia 400 is a masterpiece that truly defines the standard for modern high-speed negative film. It is the biggest beneficiary of the fourth photosensitive layer technology. It can maintain extremely precise color balance under indoor fluorescent lights, dusk or complex mixed light sources, greatly reducing the probability of color cast. The combination of its light-sensitive speed and fine grain has reached a perfect singularity, making it not only capable of high-speed capture, but also capable of providing clear, saturated images in low-light environments. It is the ultimate solution for news, street documentary and all-weather photography, and is the core representative of Fujifilm’s green power in the global imaging market.

name: Superia Premium 400
description: Fujifilm Superia Premium 400 is a high-sensitivity color negative film created by Fujifilm for 35mm film photography enthusiasts. It is nominally ISO400, suitable for a variety of light environments, and supports the standard C-41 color negative film development process. This film is most common in the Japanese market and is often considered the "high-end" version of the Superia series due to its color performance and saturation. The Superia Premium 400's image performance features include vivid and rich colors, high-sharp details and natural skin tone reproduction, resulting in bright, well-defined images in a variety of shooting conditions. Compared with the standard Superia / Superia X‑Tra 400, its colors are richer, especially red tones, with stronger overall color tendencies and higher contrast, while the color balance under artificial light is also robust.

name: Superia X-tra 400
description: Superia X-TRA 400 is one of the world's most popular high-speed consumer negative films and the most popular carrier of "fourth photosensitive layer" technology. This film is designed to offer the ultimate in versatility: its ISO 400 sensitivity means it can be used in bright sunlight, overcast streets or indoor parties. It's known for excellent color saturation (especially Fuji's signature greens and blues) and reassuring stability. Compared with ordinary civilian rolls, its color performance under fluorescent lights is more accurate, which greatly reduces the pressure of color correction in the later stage. It is the "long-term ration" of countless travelers and street photographers, and represents the perfect combination of high cost performance and reliable image quality.

name: Superia X-tra 800
description: Superia X-TRA 800 is an "action" film built for speed and low light. In an era when digital high-sensitivity was not yet mature, it was a secret weapon for capturing high-speed sports events, indoor celebrations, and nighttime street moments. By introducing advanced fine-grain technology, Fujifilm has allowed this ISO 800 film to maintain a high sensitivity while still maintaining an amazingly tight image quality. It inherits the powerful color reproduction capabilities of the X-TRA series and can still provide bright and three-dimensional colors in low-light environments, without appearing gray like ordinary high-sensitivity rolls. Not only is it a perfect match for many zoom point-and-shoot cameras, it’s also a favorite for art photographers looking for cinematic grain and low-light ambience.

name: Trebi 400
description: Trebi 400 is a Japan-exclusive model in Fujifilm's reversal film series that combines high sensitivity and vivid colors. Its technical core largely refers to the famous Provia 400 series, but it has been specially adjusted to make its colors more vivid and brighter than Provia. It has a jumping sense of vitality, especially when expressing skin colors and natural scenery under the sun. As an ISO 400 high-sensitivity reversal film, Trebi 400 maintains excellent color saturation while still having very tight and delicate grain performance. It greatly lowers the threshold for shooting reversal films in low light, allowing photographers to still obtain transparent and highly three-dimensional positive images at dusk, indoors, or in capture scenes that require high-speed shutter speeds. Due to its special background and unique hair color tendency, it is still a collectible film coveted by many reversal film players looking for "Japanese color".

name: Velvia 100
description: Velvia 100 is a high-speed version developed to provide greater flexibility at the pace of modern photography. While inheriting the high saturation gene of the Velvia series, it significantly improves the photosensitivity speed. By introducing new coupler technology, it further enhances color purity and stability while maintaining the vividness of red and green colors. It has extremely low graininess (RMS 8), extremely sharp imaging, and has better reciprocity characteristics than Velvia 50. It is an all-round solution for landscape, ecology and macro photography, especially for professional scenes that require fast shutter speeds to capture instantaneous movement.

name: Velvia 100F
description: Velvia 100F is the advanced model in the series that pursues “color accuracy.” Although it also belongs to the high saturation family, its adjustment is more focused on finding a balance among bright colors. It uses multi-layer core-shell grain technology designed to solve the color cast problem that occurred in early high-saturation films under certain extreme lights. In comparison, the color performance of the 100F is smoother and more durable, and the contrast control is softer, making it capable of landscape expressiveness and capable of shooting some high-end products or commercial photography with strict color requirements. It is an exquisite balance between color tension and true reproduction that Fuji has found.

name: Velvia 50
description: Velvia 50 is the crown jewel of Fuji reversal films and the “magic film” in the eyes of landscape photographers around the world. As a low-sensitivity film at ISO 50, it offers ultimate resolution and almost imperceptible fine grain. Its most famous feature is its exaggerated and captivating color saturation, which can transform ordinary forest green into deep emerald green, and turn the afterglow of sunset into intense flame red. The contrast is huge, and the capture of light and shadow is extremely dramatic. When held in the hand, each negative is like a piece of stained glass with concentrated colors. Although it has an extremely narrow exposure latitude and is sensitive to reciprocity failures, this is why it is known as the "touchstone for professional photographers."

name: Venus 400
description: Venus 400 is Fujifilm's flagship 400-degree negative film. It adopted the most advanced particle arrangement technology at the time, aiming to break the law that "high-speed scrolling images must be rough". The image of this film is very clear, and the color reproduction has the usual transparency of Japanese special rolls. The rendering of greens and blues is particularly charming. Compared with the global version of Superia 400, Venus 400's skin color is more rosy and natural, and the contrast is adjusted to be smoother. It is an excellent "humanistic scroll" that can capture the subtle light in the air and maintain an extremely clean picture even in cloudy or low-light environments. It is regarded by many street sweeping enthusiasts as the pinnacle of image quality among 400-degree civilian scrolls.

name: Venus 800
description: Venus 800 is an 800-degree color negative film recognized as one of the “most detailed ever produced.” Its appearance completely changed the texture of indoor and night photography. Thanks to Fujifilm's fine-grain emulsion technology, it's even grainier than many common brands of 400-degree film. The Venus 800 has an amazing latitude and is able to maintain vivid colors when handling details in extremely dark areas without severe graying or color collapse. Its unique color depth can give night scene photos a deep and romantic atmosphere. Whether you are shooting urban neon at night or capturing warm moments indoors where flash is not possible, Venus 800 is an irreplaceable high-sensitivity film in the hands of film players.

name: Phoenix 200
description: Harman Phoenix is ​​an innovative ISO200 color negative film launched by Harman Technology in 2023, marking the company's new attempt to enter color photography from the traditional black and white film field. The first color film to be designed, coated and rolled entirely by Harman at its Mobberley plant in England, it utilizes the standard C-41 color negative processing process. The original Phoenix image has obvious graininess, high contrast, and strong color expression. It can show rich greens, reds, and blues in a well-lit environment. At the same time, an obvious halation effect may appear under bright light sources, giving the image a distinct, period-feeling film aesthetic. Although the color balance and latitude are different from mainstream film, and even more experimental and unpredictable, its unique visual style and "pure analog" feel provide a creative experience that is completely different from common color films.

name: Phoenix II 200
description: Harman Phoenix II is a comprehensive upgrade and re-creation of the original Phoenix, launching in 2025. Phoenix II also uses ISO200 C-41 color negative film design. Compared with the original version, every layer of emulsion, dye and developer coupler has been redesigned to improve color reproduction, contrast control, grain fineness and sharpness, making images easier to scan and adjust in post, while retaining analogue characteristics. Phoenix II's color performance is more natural, contrast is more stable, highlight and shadow details are better preserved, and it has a wider exposure tolerance, but it still maintains a unique visual style that is different from traditional commercial color films. This film is suitable for daily portraits, landscapes, street photography and other scenes, especially if you want to create photography with an experimental film texture. Although more stable and easier to use than the first generation, Phoenix II still encourages accurate exposure for optimal results and maintains a creative style in image characteristics.

name: Red 125
description: Harman RED 125 is an ISO 125 Redscale color negative film launched by Harman Technology in the UK. It is based on the company's Phoenix series emulsions (such as Phoenix 200) and is reverse-rolled to produce a unique red scale (Redscale) image effect. The so-called Redscale means that the film is loaded into the film barrel in reverse, so that the light first passes through the film base and then enters the red photosensitive layer, so that the picture mainly shows red, orange and yellow tones, creating an experimental and visually impactful effect. As a medium-speed red-scale film, RED 125 can be processed using standard C-41 color negative processing procedures, making it suitable for most laboratories and home processors.

name: B&W Camera HP5 Plus
description: Focusing on classic black and white photography, the Ilford HP5 Plus disposable camera houses the world-renowned Ilford HP5 film. It is known for its charming coarse grain, strong tones and extremely high tolerance, and can take photos with a very artistic and documentary style. For photographers who want to experiment with the look of black and white film, this is a convenient tool to get professional tones without any setup.

name: B&W Camera XP2 Super
description: The Ilford XP2 Super disposable camera focuses on convenient and practical black and white film photography. It has built-in classic Ilford XP2 Super ISO400 film, which is characterized by fine grain, balanced and soft tones, and excellent environmental adaptability. It supports C41 process processing, which is very convenient for daily washing. With the built-in flash, it can handle most indoor and outdoor shooting scenes. It can take natural and atmospheric black and white photos without complicated adjustments. It is a worry-free choice for novices to get started with black and white film, record daily life and documentary creations.

name: Delta 100
description: Ilford Delta 100 is a high-resolution black and white film launched by Ilford, known for its extremely fine grain and excellent sharpness. The low sensitivity of ISO 100 ensures excellent detail performance and precise tone control, making it ideal for shooting in well-lit environments. Delta 100 has medium contrast and rich grayscale gradations, delivering the texture and layering of traditional black and white photos. It performs stably in a variety of developers and is suitable for landscape, architecture, still life and high-resolution creations. It is also loved by darkroom enthusiasts and technical photographers. As the representative of high-resolution film, Delta 100 is the best choice for photographers who pursue detailed images.

name: Delta 3200
description: Ilford Delta 3200 is a high-sensitivity black and white film designed for low-light environments and high-speed shooting. The high sensitivity of ISO 3200 allows photographers to obtain usable and high-quality images in night scenes, indoors, performances and low-light conditions. The Delta 3200 has noticeable but refined graininess and rich grayscale gradations, with moderate contrast, capable of creating cinematic and atmospheric black and white images. This film has extremely high tolerance and supports exposure push. It is suitable for documentary, portrait, stage and experimental creations. It is an effective film choice for darkroom enthusiasts and creators in extreme light environments.

name: Delta 400
description: Ilford Delta 400 is a medium-speed black and white film that combines versatility with film quality. A sensitivity of ISO 400 provides flexibility in a variety of lighting conditions while maintaining excellent detail and grayscale. Delta 400 has a classic grain structure and medium contrast, capable of presenting rich black and white tones and traditional film textures, making it suitable for street photography, portraits, documentary and daily creative photography. This film has excellent latitude, can support slight pushing, and has stable development. It is an ideal choice for photography enthusiasts and darkroom creators.

name: FP4 Plus
description: Ilford FP4 Plus is a classic low-speed black-and-white negative film launched by Ilford. As one of the representative products of traditional black-and-white photography, it is very popular among photography enthusiasts and professional photographers for its excellent resolution and clear tonal levels. The film has a nominal sensitivity of ISO 125 and is suitable for shooting in well-lit or controlled light environments, showing an extremely fine grain structure and excellent detail performance. FP4 Plus has a medium contrast ratio and a wide grayscale range, with fully preserved highlights and robust shadow details. The overall image texture is soft and layered, making it ideal for shooting subjects such as landscapes, architecture, still lifes, and portraits that require fine tone control. It performs stably under various developers and development schemes, maintaining consistency and good imaging results whether it is standard processing or experimental darkroom processing. As part of Ilford’s classic product line, FP4 Plus has become one of the indispensable basic films in traditional black and white film photography due to its durability, versatility and excellent image quality. It is the first choice for photographers who pursue pure black and white image texture and technical performance.

name: HP5 Plus
description: Ilford HP5 Plus is Ilford's classic black and white film and one of the most popular black and white films in the world. The ISO 400 sensitivity makes it highly versatile and can deliver excellent performance in both bright and low light environments. HP5 Plus has excellent latitude and supports exposure pushing to ISO 3200, which is very suitable for street photography, news and documentary photography. This film has classic grain and rich grayscale gradations, creating the look and feel typical of traditional black and white photos. HP5 Plus also performs stably in various developers, making it a good partner for darkroom enthusiasts. As Ilford's signature product, HP5 Plus is the best choice for black and white film.

name: Ilfochrome 100
description: Ilfochrome 100 is Ilfo's return to the pinnacle of color photography. As an ISO 100 color reversal film, its tone style is very unique: it does not have the overly exaggerated contrast of Fuji Velvia, nor is it absolutely neutral like Kodak E100, but inherits the "delicate and thick" texture of the Ilford brand. Its color saturation is adjusted to be very "European" - deep, elegant and layered. It shows excellent purity when processing reds and blues, which allows it to present a gem-like transparent three-dimensional sense when shooting cultural landscapes and high-end fashion photography.

name: Ilfocolor 400 Plus Vintage Tone
description: Ilfocolor 400 Plus is Ilfo's modern color negative product launched during the film renaissance movement. Its name pays homage to the Ilfocolor history of the 1960s, but at its core it's a new generation of film tuned for today's young film players. As a medium-speed negative film at ISO 400, it exhibits a nostalgic and soft tonal style, with a slight "vintage film feel". Its color reproduction is more natural, not as radical as modern Ektar, but with a warm orange-yellow tone and slightly rough but textured grains. It has a very good exposure latitude and is especially suitable for shooting retro humanities, warm sunny afternoons or everyday clips with a strong cinematic feel. It is Ilfo’s warm and respectful “ticket” to the world of color after many years of working in black and white.

name: Ortho Plus
description: Ilford Ortho Plus 80 is a special orthochromatic black and white film launched by Ilford, with a nominal ISO80/20°. It is not sensitive to red light and is only sensitive to blue and green light, so it has unique visual characteristics in image performance. This film is noted for its extremely fine grain structure and outstanding sharpness, making it suitable for landscapes, architecture, portraits and detailed creative photography. Since red parts (such as red clothing, brick walls, or flowers) are not sensitive to red light, they will appear as a deeper gray tone or close to black in the final image, creating a different contrast and drama than ordinary black and white film.

name: PAN 100
description: Ilford Pan 100 is a classic low-speed black-and-white negative film launched by Ilford Company. It has a nominal ISO100/21° sensitivity and is suitable for shooting in well-lit environments. It can present clear and delicate details and a traditional black-and-white image style. This film uses a full-color emulsion design, has medium contrast and a wide grayscale range, smooth imaging, and fine grains, and is suitable for photography of various subjects such as portraits, landscapes, and still lifes. Pan 100 has good latitude and can achieve excellent printing effects under appropriate development and exposure conditions. It is a classic and easy-to-use black and white film choice.

name: PAN 400
description: Ilford PAN 400 is a medium-speed black-and-white negative film with a nominal ISO400/27° sensitivity, suitable for use in low-light conditions, fast-moving scenes, and daily shooting. PAN 400 has a more obvious grain structure and good sharpness. The contrast is medium to high and the grayscale is rich. It is suitable for street photography, documentary, portrait and daily recording. This film has a wide exposure latitude, which can easily achieve stable imaging in different lighting environments. It also has a certain amount of space for pushing and processing, which can meet the needs of shooting in creative or challenging environments.

name: PAN F
description: Pan F is a classic slow panchromatic film in Ilford's history. It was born out of the need for precision photography, technical photography, and top-notch architectural photography. As an ISO 50 low-sensitivity volume, it defined the upper limit of "delicacy" in the mid-20th century. It has a very hard tone and is slightly more contrasty than modern versions, producing an extremely deep and pure black. Its silver salt coating has a very solid texture and was the best choice for that era of photographing precision parts, scientific sectioning, and artistic photography that required huge enlargements in post-production.

name: PAN F Plus
description: Pan F Plus is one of the lowest-sensitivity, finest-grained black-and-white films currently available. It is an evolution of the old version of Pan F. By improving the emulsion technology, it can greatly improve the continuity and delicacy of tones while maintaining ultimate resolution. The picture it presents is as smooth as a mirror, with almost no particles felt, giving it a "surreal" sense of transparency. It is extremely greedy in the expression of textures, whether it is the cracks in rocks or the flow of silk, it can be accurately captured. For landscape photographers and portrait photographers who pursue the ultimate in image quality, the Pan F Plus is an irreplaceable tool that allows the 135 format to have stunning depth of detail.

name: SFX 200
description: SFX 200 is a specialty black and white negative film with a sensitivity range extending into the infrared spectrum (up to 740nm). Its greatest charm lies in its special color conversion logic: with specific filters, it can produce the famous "Wood Effect" - making plant leaves containing chlorophyll appear bright white like snow, while turning the blue sky into a deep, almost black tone. Even if you don't use a deep red filter, because it is extremely sensitive to red light, the skin color of the portraits shot will appear extra white and transparent, and the flaws will be naturally faded. It has moderate contrast and a grainy texture with Ilfo’s consistent toughness, making it ideal for shooting portraits full of surrealism, dreamlike landscapes and dramatic conflicts.

name: XP2 Super
description: Ilford XP2 Super 400 is a special ISO400 black and white negative film produced by Ilford, a subsidiary of Harman Technology in the UK. It uses a dye-imaging (chromogenic) black and white emulsion and can be processed through the standard C-41 color negative film processing process. This makes it very convenient in practice: it can be processed by almost all photo labs and photo labs, without the need for special black and white chemicals. XP2 Super is known for its fine grain, crisp sharpness and extremely wide exposure latitude. It can still maintain rich image effects in scenes with large changes in lighting conditions or high contrast. Clear highlights and solid shadow details make works easier to print and scan. The film delivers balanced sharpness and grain at its optimum EI 400, while push-pull exposure to EI 50–800 allows for controlled variations in different image styles without changing the standard C‑41 development process.

name: PAN 100
description: Kentmere 100 is an ISO100 low-speed full-color black and white negative film suitable for traditional black and white photography in well-lit conditions. This film has fine grain and good sharpness, and can present a wide range of grayscale and natural contrast, making it suitable for landscapes, portraits, still life and daily photography. It has a wide exposure latitude, is beginner-friendly, and performs reliably in standard black and white development processes, making it a budget-friendly and versatile entry-level option. Kentmere 100's image quality is clear and traditional, making it an ideal film for photographers who want to practice darkroom printing or pursue the texture of classic black and white images.

name: PAN 200
description: Kentmere 200 is an ISO200 medium speed black and white negative film that sits in the middle speed position of the Kentmere series, combining contrast performance and operational flexibility. The film has enhanced contrast, well-controlled grain and good sharpness, and performs stably when light conditions change, making it suitable for street photography, portraits, travel and everyday subjects. Compared with the 100 version, it is easier to achieve ideal exposure in medium light; compared with the 400 version, the contrast and details are more balanced. Kentmere 200 also supports standard black and white development processes and achieves controllable results with most developers.

name: PAN 400
description: Kentmere 400 is an ISO400 high-speed black and white negative film with higher sensitivity and wider exposure tolerance for use in low light, dynamic scenes or fast-paced shooting. The film has obvious yet textured grain, good contrast and a wide gray scale range. It performs stably in standard black and white development processing, making it a practical choice for street photography, documentary, portrait and multi-scene creations. Compared with the 100 version, the grain of the 400 is slightly stronger, but it is easier to obtain usable images in low-light environments; compared with the medium-speed 200 version, the higher ISO makes it more suitable for dynamic and low-light subjects.

name: 100 TMAX
description: T-Max 100 is a classic ISO 100 black and white negative film, famous for its extremely fine T-Grain emulsion, with extremely low grain, excellent sharpness and resolution. The contrast levels are clean and sharp, the grayscale transition is smooth, the dark parts are pure, and the bright parts are controllable. It has excellent tolerance and push-pull performance, and is suitable for landscapes, portraits and high-precision creations. It is the first choice for black and white in pursuit of details and "calm texture".

name: 400 TMAX
description:
The T-Max 400 is a legendary model in black and white negative film. It is equipped with the iconic T-Grain technology, which breaks through the limitations of traditional grains and achieves the perfect balance of extremely high definition and delicate texture.
As an ISO 400 medium-speed film, it performs stably in changing light environments, has sufficient sensitivity to deal with low light, and retains rich tonal levels. Its contrast is soft and its tolerance is excellent, leaving plenty of room for flushing. Whether it is street documentaries, portraits or travel records, it can present sharp and three-dimensional silver halide images.

name: 800 Film for Single Use Camera
description: The Kodak 800 is a disposable film camera with a built-in ISO 800 color negative film. It focuses on high sensitivity and a convenient experience of shooting and using. This film has good imaging capabilities in low light and indoor environments, high exposure latitude, and strong tolerance to light changes. The overall color continues Kodak's consistent style, with naturally warm tones, friendly skin tones, and relatively obvious graininess but with a unique film texture. It is suitable for parties, night scenes, travel and daily shooting. It can record real and atmospheric moments without additional settings. It is a practical choice for getting started with film photography and recording life easily.

name: ColorPlus 200
description: Kodak ColorPlus 200 is an economical color negative film launched by Kodak. It has become a popular choice for entry-level film due to its excellent cost performance and vivid colors. The universal sensitivity of ISO 200 is suitable for a variety of lighting conditions, providing good performance both outdoors and indoors. This film has high color saturation, showing warm and vivid tones, which is especially suitable for shooting portraits, travel and daily life. ColorPlus 200 has fine grain and good latitude, and you can get satisfactory results even with slightly inaccurate exposure. As one of Kodak's classic film series, ColorPlus 200 is the first choice for many people to learn film photography and is also a reliable partner for daily shooting.

name: Double-X 5222/250
description: Eastman Double-X 5222 is a legendary black-and-white film negative and one of the longest-serving emulsions in the film industry. Its sensitivity is ISO 250 in daylight and ISO 200 in light. This film is known for its wide grayscales, deep shadows, and film-like grain. Different from ordinary civilian black and white rolls, Double-X has extremely high tolerance and unique micro-contrast performance, which can create a tough and dramatic picture like the black and white clips of "Schindler's List" or "Oppenheimer". It is the first choice for professional photographers pursuing the ultimate film quality. Whether it is street documentary shooting or studio portrait shooting, it can show a deep and story-telling black and white tension.

name: E100
description: Ektachrome E100 is the 21st century culmination of Kodak reversal film technology (including current versions). It is known for its extremely natural, balanced color reproduction and fine graininess. Compared with the coldness of Fuji reversal film, the tone of E100 is more neutral and full of vitality, especially when showing clear sky, water surface and delicate skin color, it has an unparalleled sense of transparency. It is the only Kodak reversal film currently in production on the market. Its ultra-high resolution and excellent scanning performance make it an all-round choice for everything from commercial photography to starry sky photography.

name: E100 G
description: The "G" in E100G stands for "Great Grain". It's engineered for the ultimate in detail and designed to deliver mirror-smooth images. The color tendency of this film is very neutral, with almost no unnecessary color cast, and it can record the light and shadow of the shooting scene most realistically. Its highlight performance is very soft and the tones transition is smooth. It is the ultimate tool for documentary photographers who pursue realistic records and commercial photographers who need a lot of room for adjustment in post-production.

name: E100 GX
description: E100GX is the warmer version of E100G, with the "X" meaning "Extra Warm". While maintaining the extremely fine grain of the G series, Kodak has slightly increased its color temperature performance, giving it an attractive, slightly warm tone in daylight. It's perfect for shooting in the morning or on a cloudy day when the light is slightly cooler, and can inject a sun-like warmth into the picture. It's perfect for portraits and warm landscapes, making skin tones look healthier and more youthful.

name: E100 S
description: The E100S is a professional reversal film launched in the late 1990s. The "S" stands for "Saturated". It is designed to enhance the vividness of colors without distortion. While it's not as exaggerated as Velvia, it does a much better job with the reds and blues than a regular feature film. Its graininess was at the top level at the time, and its images were sharp and impactful. It was a favorite for fashion magazines, product photography, and bright outdoor shots.

name: E100 SW
description: E100SW is the warm variant of E100S, "SW" standing for "Saturated Warm". It combines bright colors with warm tones and is designed to simulate a "golden hour" visual effect. It can effectively offset the cyan-blue tones in shadows or high color temperature environments, giving landscapes and characters a full, warm texture. For those landscape photographers who think E100S is too cold and Velvia is too fake, E100SW is the perfect middle point in their minds.

name: E100 VS
description: E100VS is the "heavy weapon" in Kodak's reversal film family. "VS" stands for "Vivid Color, Silica Technology". It is a high-saturation volume launched by Kodak to directly challenge Fuji Velvia. Its color is extremely rich and the contrast is strong, which can produce a very intense visual effect. Although the graininess is slightly more obvious than that of the E100G, the powerful color performance makes it a must-have for extreme sports, wildlife and exotic landscape photography.

name: E200
description: E200 is a legendary high-sensitivity reversal film. Not only does it perform exceptionally well at a nominal ISO 200, it's also known for its astonishing "rush" capabilities. By increasing the development time, it can easily reach sensitivities of ISO 800 or higher and still maintain a very natural color balance. It is a powerful tool for astrophotographers to capture nebulae, and is also a professional guarantee for handheld photography in weak light. Its warm tone and excellent low-light response make it unique among high-sensitivity feature films.

name: EXR 5245/50D
description: EXR 5245/50D is the finest-grained and sharpest daylight color negative film in the EXR series. As the "daylight standard" for Hollywood blockbusters in the 1990s, it can present extremely pure images and solid color saturation in sufficient sunlight. It is the first choice for shooting outdoor scenery and special effects composites that pursue extreme details and no graininess.

name: EXR 5248/100T
description: EXR 5248/100T is a classic light-type color negative film designed for studio artificial light. It is known for its extremely balanced grayscale and natural color reproduction, providing a perfect balance between low and medium perception. Its tones are steady and elegant, making it a prime choice for shooting indoor dramas and exquisite portraits.

name: EXR 5287/Ultra Latitude 200T
description: EXR 5287/200T is a unique medium-sensitivity light negative film that deliberately enhances contrast and color saturation while maintaining a sensitivity of 200 degrees. This slightly "tough" visual style makes it particularly outstanding in expressing tense dramatic conflicts and modern urban night scenes.

name: EXR 5293/200T
description: EXR 5293/200T pursues ultimate tolerance and soft image texture. It has extremely fine grain expression and an extremely wide exposure range, smoothly capturing all details from highlights to shadows. It is widely regarded as one of the most versatile and post-processing models in the EXR series.

name: EXR 5296/500T
