description: The EXR 5296/500T was a breakthrough in high-sensitivity photography in the early 1990s. As one of the most advanced high-sensitivity film reels at the time, it allowed photographers to shoot in dim natural light or city nightlight. It has a charming grain full of age and deep dark parts, ushering in the "low-light narrative" era of film photography.

name: EXR 5298/500T
description: EXR 5298/500T further optimizes the grain structure and dark details. It was the high-speed roll most commonly used in Hollywood blockbusters in the mid-1990s, maintaining astonishing picture clarity in extremely low-light conditions. Its wide latitude makes it the perfect choice for shooting action blockbusters and complex light and shadow scenes.

name: Ektachrome 100 Plus
description: Ektachrome 100 Professional (EPP) is one of the most successful and longest-serving professional color reversal films in Kodak's history and was the industry standard for commercial, product and publication photography worldwide. It is known for its extremely neutral color reproduction and near-perfect "what you see is what you get" performance, without any exaggerated saturation or color casts. EPP is unique in that its emulsion layer is precisely tuned for studio lighting conditions, allowing it to accurately capture complex fabric textures, metallic textures, and natural skin tones. For still life photographers who require exacting color control, EPP is synonymous with accuracy. Although its graininess was later surpassed by newer models such as the E100G, its solid, steady tonal texture is still regarded as the pinnacle memory of traditional large-format and commercial film photography.

name: Ektachrome 5294/100D
description: Eastman Ektachrome 100D (5294) is a professional-grade color reversal film negative designed for use in daylight environments. As a masterpiece of Kodak's feature film series, it is known for its extremely high color saturation, deep black performance and extremely fine grain. At a sensitivity of ISO 100, 5294 can present a very "cinematic" transparent tone, and its blue and green performance is particularly charming, as if the real world is filtered into a gorgeous screen dream. Unlike ordinary negative film, as a reversal film, it has a lower latitude and requires extremely precise exposure control, but the reward is unparalleled sharpness and color purity. Whether used for 16mm/35mm film shooting or separated for flat photography, it is the ultimate choice for pursuing ultimate visual impact and retro film texture.

name: Ektachrome 64T
description: Kodak Ektachrome 64 is a professional daylight color reversal film renowned in film history for its stunning color accuracy and extremely fine grain. ISO 64 sensitivity makes it the first choice for commercial studios, fashion magazines and detailed landscape photography. This film pursues "ultimate realism" in color expression. It is not over-saturated like some reversal films, but presents a natural, transparent and highly textured tone, especially when restoring natural skin colors and complex cloth textures. Although it has extremely high exposure requirements (narrow latitude), once accurately exposed, it produces slides with unparalleled clarity and three-dimensionality. It is the pinnacle of film photography’s pursuit of “industrial standard” image quality.

name: Ektacolor PRO 160
description: Kodak Ektacolor Pro 160 is the latest professional-grade color negative film launched by Kodak in 2026 for the mass market. Widely regarded as the same-emulsion version of the legendary film Portra 160, this film retains the fine grain of ISO 160 while being optimized for modern scanning processes. This film inherits Kodak's signature warm tones and extremely natural skin tone reproduction, and can present soft contrast and a transparent picture under sufficient light. Its latitude is stable and it is very suitable for portrait photography, wedding documentary and daily high-quality recording. For those film enthusiasts who pursue professional-level image quality but also want higher cost performance, the new version of Ektacolor Pro 160 allows more people to experience Kodak’s delicate color aesthetics.

name: Ektacolor PRO 400
description: Kodak Ektacolor Pro 400 is Kodak's "all-round" professional color negative film relaunched in 2026, aiming to provide photographers with a more cost-effective high-end shooting solution. This film is widely considered to be the same emulsion version of the legendary film Portra 400. It has extremely fine grain and amazing sharpness, maintaining extremely high picture purity even at a sensitivity of ISO 400. Known for its excellent skin tone reproduction and wide exposure latitude, Ektacolor Pro 400 easily handles challenges ranging from harsh sunlight to low-light environments. Its tone is natural and balanced, with Kodak's signature warmth. It is an irreplaceable "golden benchmark" for wedding, documentary and street photography photographers.

name: Ektacolor PRO 800
description: Kodak Ektacolor Pro 800 is a high-performance, high-sensitivity professional color negative film relaunched in 2026 by Kodak. A modern evolution of Portra 800 technology, it's designed for low-light environments and high-speed action shots. With its amazing exposure latitude and warm and delicate tones, this film has become the best choice for indoor photography, dusk street photography and wedding scenes. Despite the high sensitivity of ISO 800, it maintains excellent sharpness and fine grain. Ektacolor Pro 800 presents Kodak's unique greasy feel and true skin color in color performance, and can capture rich shadow details under low light. It is the ultimate weapon for professional photographers when challenging the extreme light and shadow, making film photography also come to life at night.

name: Ektacolor Pro 160
description: Ektacolor Pro 160 was one of Kodak's most successful professional color negative films of the 1990s and the spiritual predecessor of the modern Portra series. Designed specifically for portrait photography, this film is set at ISO 160 and is designed to provide more flexible shutter combinations than 100-degree film while maintaining extremely fine grain. It is known for its extremely soft contrast, wide highlight latitude and unparalleled reproduction of skin tones. When processing the white details of the wedding dress and the shadows of the characters' faces, Ektacolor Pro 160 showed amazing tonal smoothness and was able to present a satin-like skin texture. It was the designated roll for studio shoots, high-end portraits, and commercial photos of the era, and defined the visual thickness of professional portrait photography in the 1990s.

name: Ektar 100
description: The Ektar 100 is the most durable model in the Ektar family. The current version (after 2008) uses Kodak's motion picture film's VISION technology to achieve smooth tones that are unimaginable under civilian sensitivities. Its colors are extremely vivid with a slight blue tinge (especially in the shadows), giving it a modern, cool quality when photographing landscapes, travel and architecture. It is the finest-grained color negative film (RMS 25) currently in production in the world. Its huge scanning potential and post-processing space make it the premier landscape film for film photographers in the digital era.

name: Ektar 1000
description: Ektar 1000 is Kodak's bold exploration of "the coexistence of high speed and image quality." In an era when ultra-high-sensitivity films were generally coarse-grained, the Ektar 1000 attempted to improve imaging quality in low light through the series' fine-grain technology. Although its graininess cannot be compared with its low-sensitivity counterparts, it still maintains good color depth and contrast at the top speed of ISO 1000. It is a powerful tool for shooting fast sports, night sports and low-light documentaries, making it possible for photographers to still obtain high-quality negative films with "Ektar blood" in extremely dark environments.

name: Ektar 125
description: The Ektar 125 was the “backbone” of the Ektar family in the early 1990s. It maintains the high-sharp, low-grain characteristics of the series while providing more flexible shooting possibilities than 25-degree rolls. Its color reproduction is very solid, and the contrast is adjusted just right, retaining rich shadow details and providing bright highlight performance. It was the "everyday roll" for many professional photographers who pursued the ultimate in image quality but did not want to be completely limited by a tripod. It performed particularly well when shooting human geography and outdoor portraits.

name: Ektar 25
description: Ektar 25 is a monument in the history of the film industry and was once hailed as "the finest-grained color negative film in the world." Thanks to the extremely low sensitivity of ISO 25, it has virtually no visible grain and is able to capture breathtaking microscopic details. Its imaging is extremely sharp, with rich color saturation and sharp contrast, making it ideal for shooting grand natural landscapes or high-precision commercial still lifes with the support of a tripod. It is the ultimate weapon developed by Kodak to challenge the clarity of reversal film. Even today, it is still the ceiling of image quality in the minds of many enthusiasts.

name: Elitechrome 100
description: Kodak Elite Chrome 100 is a consumer-grade daylight color reversal film designed for photography enthusiasts. It features Kodak's famous T-GRAIN emulsion technology, which delivers ultra-fine grain and stunning image sharpness while maintaining ISO 100 sensitivity. Known for its natural, vivid color reproduction and exceptional skin tone representation, this film is ideal for everyday recordings, travel landscapes, and outdoor portraits. Compared with the professional version of Ektachrome, Elite Chrome 100 has a more lively tone, solid performance in dark areas, and a transparent texture in highlights. It is a representative of the classic reversal film in the golden age of film that combines high performance and cost-effectiveness.

name: Elitechrome 100 Extracolor
description: Kodak Elite Chrome Extra Color 100 (EBX) is a consumer-grade color reversal film that pursues ultimate color performance. It's an "enhanced version" of Kodak's Ektachrome expertise and is designed for photographers who crave vivid, eye-catching color. At a sensitivity of ISO 100, EBX displays amazing color saturation, especially when expressing clear blue skies, emerald green vegetation, and deep reds, with a strong visual impact. Its extremely fine grain and sharpness produce clear, brilliant slides not only under standard E-6 processing.

name: Fun Saver
description: Kodak FunSaver is a color disposable film camera focused on easy daily recording, with built-in Kodak ISO 800 Color film has bright, soft and warm colors full of life. The grains are fine and natural. It has stable performance in daylight, cloudy days and indoor low light. It is equipped with a fixed wide-angle lens and built-in flash. No parameter settings are required. Focus, exposure and flash are fully integrated. Automated operation, ready to use, suitable for various scenes such as travel, parties, daily shooting, etc. For entry-level players and ordinary recorders who want to easily experience the quality of film and don’t want to fiddle with equipment, it is a simple, reliable, and full-of-atmosphere portable shooting tool.

name: Gold 100
description:
Gold 100 is a classic entry-level color negative film. ISO100 sensitivity is suitable for outdoor scenes with sufficient light, with delicate color reproduction and moderate graininess.
Its biggest feature is its warm tones, especially the skin tones of portraits, which will have a unique golden sheen, creating a soft and nostalgic atmosphere. As a Tiger Balm film, it is suitable for landscape photography and is also the best choice for novices to practice exposure control.
Using standard C-41 process, flushing is easy and cost-effective. Although the recipe has been tweaked over time, the signature "Kodak flavor" remains captivating. Whether recording daily life or creating creative works, Gold 100 is a cost-effective partner for capturing beautiful moments and is worth trying.

name: Gold 200
description: Gold 200 is one of Kodak's most classic and popular everyday color negative films. The universal sensitivity of ISO 200 makes it suitable for a variety of shooting scenes, from outdoor sunlight to indoor environments, and can deliver good performance. This film is known for its warm, vibrant tones, which give photos a retro, nostalgic feel. Gold 200 restores natural skin tones and is especially suitable for portraits, street photography and travel photos. This film is affordable and has stable performance. It is one of the best-selling films in the world. Gold 200 carries the memories and stories of countless people. It is a classic representative of film photography and the daily first choice of many photographers.

name: Gold 400
description:
Gold 400 is Kodak's classic general-purpose color negative film, processed using the standard C-41 process. Its ISO 400 sensitivity enables excellent performance in both natural light and indoor environments, balancing speed and image quality.
The biggest feature of this film is that the colors are warm and saturated, the highlights are softly transitioned, the shadows are rich in detail, and the iconic grainy texture creates a unique retro atmosphere. Whether it is daily street sweeping, portrait photography or travel scenery, it can provide stable and emotional images under a variety of light conditions.
With its strong reputation among users, Gold 400 continues to freeze the warm and real moments in life. It is a classic medium that connects traditional photography with modern life.

name: Kodachrome 25
description: Kodachrome 25 is recognized as one of the greatest color reversal films in the history of photography, and is the sharpest and finest-grained film in Kodak's history. Thanks to its extremely low sensitivity of ISO 25, it has an almost "grain-free" pure texture and is able to capture stunning minute details. Known for its unique K-14 processing process, Kodachrome 25's imaging does not create color directly in an emulsion, but adds dye layer by layer during the processing process. This gives it deep blacks, extremely high contrast, and the kind of "timeless color" that will not fade across half a century. It's the ultimate choice for National Geographic photographers and professional artists. Although the K-14 process was officially discontinued in 2010, the richly colored, relief-like three-dimensional images it left behind remain an insurmountable benchmark for film photography.

name: Kodacolor 100
description: Kodak Kodacolor 100 is a low-speed ISO 100 daylight-balanced color negative film launched by Kodak in 2025, suitable for shooting everyday images in well-lit environments. The film is processed using standard C‑41 color negative processing, resulting in fine grain, high sharpness and saturated yet natural color results. Kodacolor 100 has good image latitude, taking into account both highlight and dark details under bright light, and can present classic and stable color reproduction, making it suitable for landscapes, portraits, travel and daily creations. Its consistent color performance and ease of use make it a practical choice for photographers who want to experience film photography or for shooting general scenes.

name: Kodacolor 200
description: Kodak Kodacolor 200 is an ISO 200 medium speed daylight balanced color negative film positioned as a more versatile color film that remains stable in low light conditions. Like the Kodacolor 100, it supports the standard C‑41 processing process, delivering fine grain and sharpness, while delivering saturated, true-to-life colors and a soft, natural imaging style. Due to its higher sensitivity, Kodacolor 200 has greater exposure tolerance in shadows or indoor environments, making it suitable for everyday shooting in street photography, portraits, events and travel scenes. Considered Kodak's reliable "everyday color negative" film, this film performs more confidently in environments with varying lighting conditions.

name: Outdoor
description: The Kodak Daylight (often referred to as the Kodak Outdoor) is Kodak's purest disposable camera, designed specifically for use in well-lit outdoor environments. Unlike models with flash, this camera removes the flash assembly in pursuit of ultimate portability and simplicity, making it more suitable for use at the beach, in the park, or on a sunny trip. It has built-in high-performance film with a sensitivity of ISO 800, which allows it to maintain a very high shooting success rate in cloudy or shadowy locations even without a flash. The precision lens it is equipped with can produce typical "Kodak Gold" tones with rich colors and sharp contrast. It is the favorite of those film lovers who advocate "capturing natural light". It is not only extremely light in weight, but also can present a pure documentary texture without additives.

name: P3200 TMAX
description: Kodak T-MAX P3200 is an extremely high-speed black and white negative film from Kodak, designed for shooting in low light, night photography and dynamic scenes. It uses T-GRAIN emulsion technology, which can maintain a relatively fine grain structure and excellent sharpness even at such high sensitivities, rather than the rough graininess of traditional high-sensitivity films. The nominal sensitivity is ISO3200/36°, but it is actually a multi-sensitivity film: under standard development conditions, its basic sensitivity is generally considered to be ISO800–1000, and it can easily reach or exceed EI3200 through push-stop processing to cope with extremely dark scenes. This means that the P3200 can still capture images stably in low light or when flash is not available, making it ideal for handheld night scenes, street photography, and fast-paced action photography.

name: Plus-x 5231
description: Eastman Plus-X 5231 is a classic sweep-second medium-sensitivity black-and-white film negative with a daylight sensitivity of ISO 80. It played a crucial role in the golden age of Hollywood black-and-white films and is known for its extremely fine grain, silky grayscale transitions and soft contrast expression. Compared with the high-sensitivity Double-X, Plus-X 5231 can provide richer and more delicate mid-tones (Mid-tones), giving the picture a creamy texture. It is the first choice for shooting classic Hollywood portraits, close-ups and indoor scenes with delicate light and shadow. Although Kodak has officially stopped producing this film around 2010, the image style it left behind, which combines retro beauty with modern sharpness, is still an irreplaceable artistic standard among black and white photography enthusiasts.

name: Portra 100 T
description: Kodak Portra 100T is a professional color negative film designed specifically for 3200K lighting environments. As the only light balancing volume in the Portra family, it is known for its extremely fine particles and precise white balance correction, which can effectively eliminate the yellow color cast under artificial light sources and present a clear, calm tone. It is a professional tool for commercial studios, high-end indoor portrait and architectural photographers who pursue ultimate image quality under lighting conditions.

name: Portra 160
description: Kodak Portra 160 is a low-speed color negative film rated ISO 160, designed for portraits and natural light photography. Its colors are balanced and natural, skin tones are restored to be warm and soft, and it also has extremely low graininess and wide gray scales, making the picture rich and delicate. Portra 160 has excellent latitude, retaining detail and color even in slightly underexposed or overexposed conditions. This film is particularly suitable for shooting portraits, landscapes and travel records in daylight, and can present warm and natural color tones and soft transitions of light and shadow effects. As one of Kodak's classic Portra series, the Portra 160 provides stable, controllable color performance in scanning or printing, making it an ideal choice for photographers pursuing detailed images and professional portrait effects.

name: Portra 160 NC
description: Kodak Portra 160NC is the pinnacle of the pursuit of "realism". As a low-contrast, neutral-color professional roll, it provides the most delicate skin tone reproduction and an extremely wide dynamic range in the film industry. NC stands for "natural color". It does not pursue exaggerated color tension, but is committed to retaining every detail in shadows and highlights. It is the most respected "king of skin colors" in wedding photography and documentary portraits.

name: Portra 160 VC
description: Kodak Portra 160VC injects more color vitality while maintaining 160-degree delicate picture quality. VC stands for "Vivid Color," which makes images brighter and more solid by increasing contrast and saturation. Although more pigmented, it still retains the Portra family's excellent complexion handling capabilities. It is the first choice for fashion and landscape photographers who want both professional and delicate textures and stronger visual impact.

name: Portra 400
description: Kodak Portra 400 is Kodak's most popular professional-grade portrait film and is hailed as the "King of Portraits" by many photographers. A sensitivity of ISO 400 provides good flexibility for a variety of lighting conditions, both indoors and outdoors. Portra 400 is known for its natural and delicate skin tone reproduction, soft color transitions and extremely fine grain structure. This film has excellent latitude and maintains excellent image quality even if there are deviations in exposure. Portra 400 is particularly suitable for wedding, portrait and fashion photography, and can present elegant and natural color styles. Enjoying a high reputation among professional photographers, Portra 400 is the benchmark product for portrait film and the first choice for many commercial photographers.

name: Portra 400 BW
description: Kodak Portra 400BW is a black and white film (dye-based black and white film) based on the C-41 processing process. It essentially builds black-and-white images on color negative film technology, resulting in an extremely wide exposure latitude and a silky texture like Portra color rolls. It can easily produce films in any color processing shop and produce black and white images with a very cinematic feel and extremely rich gray scales. It is a flexible solution for professional photographers to create black and white around the clock.

name: Portra 400 NC
description: The Kodak Portra 400NC is the “gentle” of 400-degree high-speed rolls. It provides high sensitivity enough to deal with complex light, while still maintaining low contrast and natural color tendencies. It can soften the messy light and shadow and make the skin color white and transparent. It was the “go-to roll” for countless documentary and wedding photographers in the 2000s, guaranteeing consistent, authentic professional performance in any environment.

name: Portra 400 VC
description: The Kodak Portra 400VC is a powerful all-rounder. It combines the high flexibility of ISO 400 with the rich colors that are the hallmark of the VC Series. This film can produce high-contrast images with deep dark areas and bright highlights, making it ideal for capturing dynamic city streets, colorful travel documentaries, or distinctive fashion shoots. It is the most modern and dramatic member of the Portra family.

name: Portra 800
description: Kodak Portra 800 is a high-speed color negative film rated at ISO 800 for reliable exposures in low light or indoor conditions. This film inherits the soft colors and natural skin tone reproduction of the Portra series, while maintaining low graininess at high speeds, taking into account the needs of delicate image quality and fast shooting. Portra 800 is suitable for street photography, travel, portraits and event photography. It can still show soft and natural colors and stable exposure under large light changes or low light conditions. It has high tolerance and can be flexibly processed in different light environments. It is also suitable for scanning and printing, and can present rich gray scales and layers. Portra 800 provides photographers with a reliable choice for maintaining high-quality images in complex lighting conditions.

name: Power Flash
description: The Kodak Power Flash is an all-around disposable camera designed for all-weather shooting, especially in dimly lit rooms or at night. The core advantage of this camera is its high-power flash, which can cover an ultra-wide effective range of 1.2 meters to 4.5 meters, far exceeding that of ordinary disposable cameras. It has a built-in color negative film with a sensitivity of ISO 800, and combined with a powerful flash, it can not only ensure the clarity of background details, but also eliminate the shake blur common in indoor shooting. It produces photos with rich colors and high contrast, with a typical Kodak "warm gold" tone. Whether it's a family gathering, a late-night party or an indoor event with complex lighting, Power Flash is your reliable partner that allows you to "take great photos with your eyes closed" and is the ultimate tool to capture every shining moment.

name: Pro Image 100
description: Kodak Pro Image 100 is an economical color negative film launched by Kodak. The low-speed sensitivity of ISO 100 ensures good image quality and detailed performance. Popular for its excellent value for money and vivid colors, this film is particularly suitable for everyday photography and travel photos. The color saturation of Pro Image 100 is higher, showing warm and bright tones, suitable for outdoor environments with sufficient light. This film has fine grain and good latitude, making it a good choice for entry-level photography enthusiasts. Although positioned as a basic-level film, the image quality and color performance of Pro Image 100 are sufficient to meet most shooting needs. It is especially popular in the Asian market and is a practical choice for daily recording and travel photography.

name: Profoto XL
description: Kodak Profoto XL 100 is an entry-level professional color negative film designed for professional portrait and commercial photography. As a cost-effective member of Kodak's Professional Line, it is known for its extremely fine grain and natural and transparent tones. At a sensitivity of ISO 100, Profoto XL demonstrates excellent sharpness and solid detail capture capabilities. Although it is not as expensive as the Portra series, it is not cheap in terms of color performance - it has moderate saturation, and the restoration of skin color tends to be natural and fair, with Kodak's signature slightly warm undertone. For photographers who pursue the delicate texture of professional negatives while controlling costs in high-volume shooting, the Profoto XL 100 is a near-perfect balance.

name: Sport
description: The Kodak Sport disposable waterproof camera is specially designed for outdoor and underwater adventures. It has built-in Kodak ISO 800 high-speed color film. It has a sturdy body that is waterproof to a depth of 15 meters, shockproof and scratch-resistant. It can produce bright colors, clear details, and natural skin tones in sunlight. Its high sensitivity can adapt to various outdoor lights. No complicated settings are required, just take and shoot. It is a reliable and portable choice for easily recording vivid images at the beach, swimming pool, travel and outdoor documentary shooting.

name: Super Gold 100
description: Kodak Super Gold 100 has a core emulsion based on the famous Gold 100 that has been slightly modified. It is known for its fine, silky grain and extremely high image sharpness. At a sensitivity of ISO 100, Super Gold 100 shows an amazing tonal gradation, especially when capturing landscapes and delicate portraits under bright sunlight, showing a transparent, solid and highly textured picture. Compared with the standard version of Gold, its color performance is more stable, while maintaining Kodak's signature warm tones, and the dark areas are deeper. For players who pursue the ultimate image quality details and Japanese retro filter feel, this "Super Gold" is an irreplaceable recorder under the sun.

name: Super Gold 200
description: The Kodak Super Gold 200 is the most balanced all-round model in the series, with an ISO 200 sensitivity that makes it easy to operate in different outdoor lighting conditions. This film combines Kodak's warm undertones with a unique clarity, resulting in vivid yet realistic colors. Its latitude is very robust and tolerates underexposure or overexposure well. The photos taken by Super Gold 200 often have a bright atmosphere, which is very suitable for street sweeping, travel documentaries and film beginners. It was a representative of the "high-quality civilian rolls" of that era, and instantly coated the lives of countless photography enthusiasts with a layer of gold that never fades.

name: T400CN
description: T400CN is a professional-grade black and white film designed for the pursuit of ultra-delicate texture and convenience in developing and printing. Unlike traditional silver salt black and white rolls (such as Tri-X), after T400CN is developed, the image on the film is composed of dye clouds (Dye Clouds) instead of rough silver particles. This gives it almost the most delicate and rounded picture performance in the ISO 400 level, without the gritty feeling of traditional high-speed rolls. Its biggest advantage is its amazing latitude, which can easily control complex light ratios from extremely bright to extremely dark. And because it comes with an orange mask, it can directly enter the C-41 machine of any color printing shop for enlargement, and obtain black and white photos with extremely accurate grayscale and soft texture on ordinary color photo paper. It was a favorite of wedding photographers, portrait photographers, and journalists who needed to get their shots out quickly.

name: TRI-X 400
description: Tri-X 400 is a landmark black-and-white film introduced by Kodak in 1954. It is the world's first true high-speed black-and-white negative film. Its appearance allows photographers to completely get rid of the shackles of flash and tripod and enter a new era of "field light" photography. Tri-X is known for its extremely wide exposure latitude and signature grain. Its particles are not the kind of fine impurities, but a texture full of power, like a charcoal sketch. Its contrasts are captivating: shadows are deep and solid, highlights are bouncy and extremely difficult to expose. What's even more legendary is its "durability" - it can shoot in almost any light, and can easily reach ISO 1600 or even 3200 by pushing, while still maintaining stunning picture performance.

name: UltraMax 400
description: Kodak UltraMax 400 is Kodak's economical everyday color negative film, and its ISO 400 sensitivity provides great versatility. This film has become one of the most popular films in the world due to its affordable price and stable performance. The colors of UltraMax 400 are vivid and saturated, showing warm and bright tones, which is especially suitable for daily photography, street photography and travel photos. This film has good grain control and excellent latitude, providing satisfactory performance in a variety of lighting conditions. As a good choice for entry-level film, UltraMax 400 is the first choice for many people to learn film photography, and it is also an economical and practical choice for daily shooting.

name: Vision1 5246/250D
description: Vision 5246/50D is the “King of Sharpness” in the Vision family. As the successor to the 5245 (EXR), it further optimizes the grain structure to deliver an extremely pure, transparent picture even under the scorching sun. Its colors are extremely solid and its reproduction of blue sky and green land has an amazing three-dimensional effect. It is the ultimate solution for shooting large-scale outdoor panoramas and high-definition special effects films.

name: Vision1 5263/Low Contrast 500T
description: The Vision 5263/250D is an extremely rare special model designed to fill the daylight gap between the low-sensitivity 50D and the high-sensitivity light volumes. It has excellent daylight balance and neutral tones while maintaining an ISO 250 sensitivity. It is ideal for use in outdoor environments such as clouds, cloudy days or forests where the lighting is complex but still needs to maintain the natural feel of daylight, providing a high degree of narrative consistency.

name: Vision1 5274/200T
description: The Vision 5274/200T is an extremely well-balanced illuminated color negative film and is considered the most versatile model in the series. It perfectly balances sensitivity and fineness, has an extremely wide exposure latitude and natural and moist skin color performance. Whether it is the exquisite lighting in the studio or the evening in the city, it can stably capture rich mid-tone details, making it a "work horse" for mainstream commercial films at the time.

name: Vision1 5277/320T
description: Vision 5277/320T is the "artistic youth" in the Vision series, known for its low contrast and soft tones. It's designed specifically for photographers looking for haziness, subtle shadow transitions, and non-linear storytelling. It can effectively soften the harsh highlights and create a slightly melancholy and textured picture atmosphere. It is a perfect shot for shooting nostalgic themes and emotional portraits.

name: Vision1 5279/500T
description: Vision 5279/500T ushered in the "era of high-speed popularization" of film photography. It was the most widely used high-sensitivity film roll in the world around 2000, and was sensitive enough to handle extremely low-light nights. Despite its high sensitivity, it still maintains excellent grain control and color saturation, providing cinematographers with the flexibility to create freely on the streets at night or in dark interiors, setting the visual tone for modern action films.

name: Vision1 5289/800T
description: Vision 5289/800T is an attempt by the Vision series to challenge the limits of light and shadow, and is specially developed for extreme dark environments. It was the most sensitive professional color film negative at the time, and its unique graininess gave the picture a strong original texture and documentary tension. It’s the ultimate “night vision” for shooting underground music, late-night documentaries, and any scene where artificial fill light isn’t available.

name: Vision2 5201/50D
description: Kodak VISION2 5201/50D is a daylight-balanced, low-sensitivity film negative known for its extremely fine grain and sharp imaging effects. As the VISION series pioneers the transition to digital, it delivers extremely pristine images in bright outdoor light. Although the highlight latitude is slightly less than that of the later 50D (5203), it has more solid color saturation and slightly stiffer detail expression. It is an ideal choice for shooting large scenes under the sun and pursuing high definition and classic film texture.

name: Vision2 5205/250D
description: Kodak VISION2 5205/250D is an all-weather daylight film negative film, which is one of the main films used in classic film history such as "The Dark Knight". It has a very natural color balance and excellent dark detail restoration capabilities, and can capture outdoor images with a great sense of space. Compared with the VISION3 version, its contrast is slightly greater and the picture is sharper. Whether it's a bright day or a cloudy afternoon, the 250D delivers that classic Hollywood color with narrative power and a hint of retro flair.

name: Vision2 5212/100T
description: Kodak VISION2 5212/100T is a light-balanced negative film that pursues the ultimate in delicate texture. It was once hailed as "the clearest color film." It displays stunningly smooth grayscale and color accuracy under 3200K tungsten lighting, with even less grain than many low-sensitivity films. It is very suitable for use in indoor studio shots with sophisticated lighting or commercial creations that require high-magnification magnification. It can present a calm, restrained and modern high-end tone.

name: Vision2 5217/200T
description: Kodak VISION2 5217/200T is a highly flexible, medium-sensitivity, light-balanced negative film used extensively in film production. It achieves a perfect balance between fineness and photosensitivity speed, and the color style is deeper than that of VISION3 200T, with a typical "early 21st century movie feel". Its restoration of skin color is extremely soft and flexible, and it also has good adaptability under mixed light sources. It is a very reliable tone carrier when shooting humanistic documentaries and indoor drama films.

name: Vision2 5218/500T
description: Kodak VISION2 5218/500T is a high-sensitivity light-type negative film that is of great significance for the times, completely changing the reliance on low light in film shooting. It maintains rich shadow levels and acceptable graininess in low light. Its tone style is melancholic and deep, with a charming blue-blue tendency in the dark parts, which is very suitable for creating the dramatic tension of night scenes. It's the perfect choice for capturing city nights, indoor candlelight, and any artistic creation that requires extreme light sensitivity.

name: Vision2 5229/Expression 500T
description:
Kodak VISION2 Expression 5229/500T is a light-balanced film negative designed specifically to pursue a specific artistic style, playing the role of "mood master" in the VISION2 family.
Unlike conventional models that pursue high contrast and high saturation, 5229 takes low contrast and low color saturation as its core features. It can present extremely soft and smooth skin tone transitions and has excellent dark detail expression, maintaining a very fine grain structure even at a photosensitive speed of 500 degrees. This characteristic gives the picture a light, alienated melancholy, which is very suitable for capturing dreamy, hazy or nostalgic narrative scenes. Kodak VISION2 Expression 500T is the advanced choice for photographers and directors who want to lay the foundation for soft tones in the early stage, reduce the digital feel in the later stage, and pursue delicate film aesthetics.

name: Vision3 5203/50D
description: Kodak VISION3 5203/50D is a daylight-balanced (5500K) low-sensitivity color film negative known for its finest grain and exceptional sharpness in the world. This film has an amazing highlight latitude, and can still retain extremely rich bright details in strong sunlight or high-contrast outdoor environments. Its color restoration is natural and true, skin color is transparent, the picture is clean and pure, and it has extremely high resolution. The 50D is suitable for landscapes, portraits or commercial creations outdoors in well-lit areas. It is the first choice for creators who pursue ultimate image quality and delicate tones when shooting on sunny days.

name: Vision3 5207/250D
description: Kodak VISION3 5207/250D is a versatile medium-sensitivity daylight-balanced color film negative that perfectly balances speed and image quality. It continues the iconic ultra-wide dynamic range of film and uses advanced dye layering technology (DLT) to significantly reduce dark grain and make shadow details clearer. Its color performance is vivid and rich in layers, and it can maintain stable tones under changing light. Suitable for most outdoor scenes from early morning to late evening, as well as indoor shooting with good lighting, 250D is an all-weather film film with a strong sense of narrative that can adapt to a variety of complex shooting tasks.

name: Vision3 5213/200T
description: Kodak VISION3 5219/200T is a light-balanced (3200K) medium-sensitivity color film negative that is optimized for artificial light environments and has a delicate structure close to that of 100-degree film. It accurately offsets the orange-yellow tint produced by tungsten lighting, delivering cool, accurate and film-like colors. With its excellent highlight control and dark performance, it performs particularly well in indoor scenes with complex light ratios; if used with the 85 filter when shooting in daylight, it will show a warm and retro tone. 200T is very suitable for indoor portraits, night streets, and stage-like light and shadow creations.

name: Vision3 5219/500T
description: Kodak VISION3 5219/500T is a legendary high-sensitivity light-balanced color film negative film that is currently one of the most widely used models in the film industry. Designed specifically for low light and challenging environments, it uses sub-micron technology to achieve delicate performance at high sensitivities, and can recover dark details through a wide dynamic range even in bold underexposure situations. Its colors are highly dramatic and can create a unique contrast between warm and cold when dealing with city neon lights, night scenes and mixed light sources. 500T is suitable for indoor low light, night scenes, and image creation that pursues high contrast and strong expressiveness. It is the ultimate tool for capturing the soul of the night.

name: Business 400
description: Konica Business 400 is a "tool-type" color negative film positioned for professional use. Its core selling point is its superior environmental adaptability. Since business photography often involves a mixture of fluorescent lights, incandescent lights and natural light, the emulsion formula of this film has enhanced tolerance to complex light sources, greatly reducing the severe green or yellow cast that is prone to occur under artificial light sources. Its contrast is adjusted to be slightly higher than that of civilian volumes, aiming to improve the legibility of text, graphics, and architectural details. Its sensitivity is set at ISO 400, ensuring adequate shutter speeds in indoor office spaces with low lighting. Although its color is not as warm and lively as Centuria, it is more solid, objective, and has an unadorned "cold record feeling". It was the industry standard for insurance claims, construction projects, and archival records of that era.

name: Centuria 100
description: Centuria 100 is the model in the series that pursues ultimate clarity and is the culmination of Konica's color aesthetic. It has extremely fine particles and silky tonal transitions, and its color reproduction is very solid. It is not as cold as Fuji, nor as bright and yellow as Kodak, but has a slightly calm and retro feel. In full daylight, it captures very rich detail. Due to its excellent imaging quality, it was not only a high-end choice for home use at the time, but was also often used to shoot exquisite scenery and commercial records. It was synonymous with "stable and reliable" in the minds of film photographers.

name: Centuria 200
description: Centuria 200 is the "all-rounder" in the Konica family, perfectly balancing light-sensing speed and picture detail. The film's design emphasizes natural optimization of skin tones, making it excellent for family gatherings and travel portraits. It is extremely tolerant and can handle a variety of light and shadow changes from bright outdoors to shaded areas. The Centuria 200's imaging has a unique "airy feel" and the tones are warm yet sharp. It was the "main volume" used by many amateurs when recording their lives in the early 2000s.

name: Centuria 400
description: Centuria 400 is a high-performance film developed for high-speed capture and changing environments. Thanks to ultra-fine grain technology, it broke the limitation that 400-degree sensitivity inevitably resulted in coarse grains, and its clarity was at the leading level at the time. This film has excellent expressive power when processing shadow details, has moderate color saturation, and can present a thick, rich visual texture. It is ideal for street snapshots, indoor documentaries, and capturing dynamic moments in low-light environments. It is the best partner for photographers who pursue efficiency without sacrificing image quality.

name: Centuria 800
description: Centuria 800 is the "high-sensitivity elite" in the series, designed for extremely dark environments and high-speed dynamics. It still maintains excellent contrast and color purity at a high speed of ISO 800, avoiding the dark feeling common in ordinary high-sensitivity rolls. Its iconic "Konica Blue" is particularly deep in night scene photography, and can outline the night lights and night colors with a very atmospheric feel. Not only is it a great tool for sports photography and night street photography, it is also used by some art photographers to create images full of tension and storytelling because of its unique grainy texture.

name: KONIPAN SS
description: Konipan SS is an ISO 100 black-and-white full-color negative film that holds an important place in the history of East Asian photography. As the backbone of the early "Sakura Brand" black and white family, it is famous for its extremely fine grains and rich tonal levels. Different from the sharp contrast pursued by later modern films, the tone expression of Konipan SS is more like a "warm feeling" of the silver salt era. Its gray gradient (Gradation) is very evenly distributed and can capture extremely small changes in light and shadow. It responds very honestly to light, maintaining a balanced aesthetic between highlights and shadows. It was the standard for Japanese realistic photography, humanistic records and studio portraits of that era. Even today, decades later, many players who dig up old film will still be amazed by its solid silver salt texture and deep black field performance.

name: New Centuria 400
description: New Centuria 400 is Konica's masterpiece in high-speed negative film technology. As the flagship model of the "New" series, it significantly improves the presentation of skin tones, allowing it to take photos of more natural and transparent skin while maintaining high sensitivity, completely getting rid of the sallow feeling that early high-sensitivity rolls easily produced. The color saturation of this film has been re-adjusted, and the three primary colors of red, green and blue are more lively. Together with its iconic "Konica Blue", the picture presents a refreshing, bright and modern feel. It has an amazing exposure latitude, which can ensure solid details from bright to dark even in point-and-shoot cameras with inaccurate light metering. It was the top civilian volume for street sweeping, recording and all-weather photography of that era.

name: New Centuria 800
description: New Centuria 800 is a professional grade consumer roll designed to capture "movement" and "shimmer". In this generation update, Konica has further compressed the graininess brought by ISO 800, making its picture detail in the first echelon among films of the same level. Its core improvement lies in its ability to adapt to complex light sources (such as the mixture of indoor light and outdoor natural light), which greatly reduces the color cast phenomenon. The color performance is rich and has strong penetrating power. Especially in dark light environments, it can set off the atmosphere of light and shadow very well. Whether it's sports events, stage photography or late-night urban exploration, the New Centuria 800 can provide film with vivid colors and outstanding resolution, making it a rare tool for photographers who pursue the ultimate high-sensitivity experience.

name: Super Centuria 100
description: Super Centuria 100 is the pinnacle of pure image quality. As the low-sensitivity model in the series, it introduces new coupler technology, bringing the purity of the picture to an unprecedented level. Its color reproduction is very vivid, especially when expressing outdoor natural light, and the highlights are transparent and bright. Compared with the early Centuria, Super Centuria 100 has reduced the slightly heavy retro feel and instead pursued a more modern and transparent tone. It's ideal for capturing high-definition landscapes and delicate skin textures, with virtually invisible graininess even when printed in large format.

name: Super Centuria 200
description: Super Centuria 200 was the most popular "hang-up roll" in Japanese supermarkets and photo labs at the time. Its design places great emphasis on "versatility" and has a very wide exposure latitude. Even if it is underexposed by 1 stop or overexposed by 2 stops, it can still produce photos with rich colors. The color tendency of this film is very pleasing, with skin tones restored with a healthy rosiness while retaining Konica's signature sky blue. Its fine graininess and neutral to warm tones make it the best partner for recording daily life, family travel and street moments. It represents the perfect balance between ease of use and image quality of consumer-grade film.

name: Super Centuria 400
description: Super Centuria 400 is an “all-weather flagship” designed for high-speed capture. Thanks to the improved emulsion structure of the Super series, it maintains stunningly smooth tones at a high sensitivity of ISO 400, even comparable to many 100-degree ordinary films. This film performs well in processing complex light and shadows and dynamic moments, with solid color reproduction and a strong sense of space. It especially enhances the performance of contrast, making the picture look more three-dimensional and sharp. It is the first choice for street photographers, documentary workers, and those who pursue high-success rate shooting. It can provide images with vivid colors and reliable image quality regardless of whether it is cloudy, sunny, cold or warm.

name: Super Centuria 800
description: Super Centuria 800 represents Konica's crowning achievement in high-sensitivity color negative film. As the "performance beast" in the series, it uses brand-new nano-particle technology, which greatly suppresses the roughness common in high-sensitivity rolls. Its color performance is extremely intense, especially in low-light environments, it can still capture delicate tonal transitions without serious color collapse. Its charming dark performance and soft processing of lights make it a useful tool for street sweeping at night, stage photography, and documentary photography under dim light. It gives the night a deep and story-telling color, and is a top tool for exploring dark details in film photography.

name: XG 400
description: Konica XG 400 is a high-performance, all-weather color negative film known for its fine grain expression and highly distinctive color style. As the main high-sensitivity model of Konishi-Roku, the ISO 400 sensitivity makes it suitable for cloudy, evening or indoor environments. The most fascinating feature of this film is its iconic "Konica Blue" - it presents a deep, slightly melancholic and transparent blue tone, while restoring skin tones with a natural whiteness. Compared with the fiery or rich competitors at the time, the tone of XG 400 was more refreshing and restrained, with a strong sense of narrative and a fresh Japanese texture. It is the "white moonlight" for photographers who capture street moments, documentary portraits, and pursue melancholy movie atmospheres.

name: Monopan 50
description: Leica Monopan 50 is a legendary low-sensitivity black-and-white negative film, custom-produced by Leica on behalf of other manufacturers. The ISO 50 sensitivity gives it extremely fine grain and amazing sharpness, perfectly utilizing the excellent resolution of Leica lenses. This film is famous for its extremely high micro-contrast and silver-salt texture, which can show extremely rich grayscale levels from deep black to transparent highlights. Its tone style is calm, thick and full of three-dimensionality, which perfectly fits the "airy feeling" and "documentary tension" pursued by Leica cameras. Although it has long been discontinued, in the eyes of black and white photography enthusiasts, it is the ultimate medium for capturing subtle changes in light and shadow, creating classic humanistic portraits and architectural art, symbolizing the golden age of highly integrated film technology and optical design.

Lomography 100 is a low-sensitivity color negative film launched by Lomography. The film is characterized by fine grain and bright, natural color expression, delivering clear, transparent images. The film sensitivity is ISO 100, which is suitable for shooting in sufficient daylight conditions, especially for subjects such as landscapes, architecture, still life and daily records. This film has stable imaging under normal sunlight conditions and rich color levels. It is often used by photography enthusiasts in shooting scenes that pursue image quality and color performance.

Lomography 400 is an ISO 400 daylight color negative film known for its high latitude and vivid colors. The overall color orientation is rich and slightly warm, with red, yellow and blue-green being active, and the contrast is relatively bright. The graininess is more present in the 400 level, forming a typical "film smell". It has high tolerance for exposure errors and is suitable for portraits, street photography and travel records. It can create a retro, vivid and slightly playful image style.

Lomography 800 is a high-sensitivity color negative film launched by Lomography, suitable for shooting in low-light environments. The film maintains stable color performance under high-sensitivity conditions and exhibits a film-like grain effect. The film sensitivity is ISO 800, which is suitable for night scenes, indoors and low-light environments. It is often used for street photography, performances and documentary themes. This film provides a reliable option for users who need to shoot at high speeds.

name: Berlin Kino
description: Lomography Berlin Kino 400 is a medium-high sensitivity black and white negative film that emphasizes usability and expressiveness in complex lighting environments. This film has good exposure latitude, relatively obvious graininess but rich structure, high contrast, clear-cut images, and a strong film image style. Berlin Kino 400 is suitable for street photography, documentary, humanities and low-light shooting. It can present black and white images with emotional tension and a sense of time. It is a black and white film choice with a distinctive style.

name: Color 92
description: LomoChrome Color 92 is an ISO400 color negative film launched by Lomography. It is inspired by the shooting style of the 1990s and is intended to evoke the nostalgia of the golden age of film. The film is designed with a unique color gradation and grain structure to produce vivid yet vintage-like colors: soft warm tones and expressive highlights in bright light, while deep, immersive blue and green tones in shadow areas contrast vividly with vivid reds. The overall image style has a distinct sense of the times and analog texture, and is suitable for street photography, portraits, travel, and creative photography that emphasizes color and atmosphere. It also supports C‑41 processing technology, making shooting and processing very convenient.

name: Earl Grey
description: Lomography Earl Gray is a classic black and white negative film from Lomography, featuring a low sensitivity positioning of ISO100 and a traditional black and white image style. The film uses a full-color emulsion design to display a wide dynamic range of deep blacks, pure whites, and rich grayscale transitions. It also has fine grain and excellent sharpness, making it suitable for shooting in well-lit environments. Earl Gray's image style favors traditional and elegant black and white expression. The strong black and white contrast combined with rich middle gray tones makes the image both impactful and without losing layered details. It is an ideal choice for street photography, portraits, landscapes and daily creations. As a standard black and white negative film, it needs to be developed using conventional black and white development processes, and can also show different image styles in your own darkroom or experimental processing.

name: Lady Grey
description: Lomography Lady Gray is a classic ISO 400 black and white negative film launched by Lomography. It is popular among film photography enthusiasts for its elegant image style and ease of use. This Lady Gray black-and-white film is designed with a full-color emulsion that has a fine grain structure and high dynamic range to perform stably in varying lighting conditions. Its image characteristics are deep black, bright white and rich grayscale transition, giving the picture a classic black and white beauty and layering. The medium sensitivity of ISO 400 makes this film suitable for both daytime shooting and usable imaging in low-light or shadow environments, providing good flexibility for street photography, portraits, daily records, and creative black-and-white photography. Compared with the Lomography Earl Gray 100 of the same brand, Lady Gray has a more moderate contrast, is easier to use in multiple scenes, and has stronger low-light performance.

name: Lobster Redscale
description: Lomography Lobster Redscale is a specialty 110-format color negative film from Lomography. It is designed using the classic Redscale exposure principle, that is, light is reversely exposed through the negative, giving the image a unique warm-toned effect. The film has a nominal ISO 200 sensitivity, suitable for shooting in well-lit daytime environments, and can be processed through the standard C-41 color negative film processing process. Due to the reverse exposure structure, the color of the image tends to be warm tones of red, orange and yellow. The atmosphere of the image is full of drama and visual impact, which is completely different from traditional color film. Depending on the lighting conditions and exposure strategy, Lobster Redscale can also display rich tones from passionate red to soft sepia and nostalgic brown, giving every frame of image the possibility of experimentation and creative expression.

name: Metropolis
description: Lomography Metropolis is a specialty color negative film from Lomography that uses an original chemical emulsion formula to present a unique urban cold-tone image style. The film supports a wide exposure range of ISO 100-400, allowing photographers to use it flexibly in different light environments while showing fine grain structure and clear texture. The colors of Metropolis tend to be weakly saturated, soft, and slightly achromatic, forming calm tones such as slight yellow-green and taupe, which together with high contrast create an image with a rich cinematic feel and urban texture. Its unique color expression gives themes such as streets, portraits, architecture, and cityscapes a more modern, editorial visual style.

name: Orca
description: Lomography Orca is a black-and-white negative film designed for 110-format cameras, with a nominal ISO 100 sensitivity and a capacity of 24 photos per roll. Orca film uses a traditional black-and-white emulsion design and requires classic black-and-white development processes. It can be developed at home or sent to a laboratory for processing. Its performance characteristics are obvious graininess, sharp contrast and rich layers. It is suitable for capturing light and shadow, texture and simple composition, especially in daylight conditions. Due to the smaller size of the 110 negative film, the grain will be more visible when the output is enlarged. This texture creates a unique retro style and artistry.

name: Potsdam Kino
description: Lomography Potsdam Kino is a black-and-white negative film inspired by German film tradition. Its image style has a strong sense of cinema and history. This film uses a full-color emulsion design with a nominal ISO 100 sensitivity, which is suitable for shooting black and white images with rich details and distinct layers in a well-lit environment. Inspired by the image aesthetics of the New German Film Movement, this film was originally used to shoot emotional black-and-white movie scenes. Its wide grayscale range and fine grain structure can produce deep and soft black and white tones. The image contrast is moderate, the details are rich, and it is both classic and artistic. It is very suitable for landscape, street photography, portraits and creative themes with emotional atmosphere.

name: Purple
description: The Lomography Purple series are experimental color negative films from Lomography, using a unique color cast emulsion design to capture unconventional color shifts in the standard C-41 color negative film processing process. The film features a flexible exposure range of variable sensitivity ISO100-400, allowing photographers to tailor performance to light and creative needs. The most notable feature of Purple film is its fantasy color cast effect: green and blue tones will shift toward purple or indigo, yellow will appear pink, while red and skin tones usually remain more realistic. This "color shift" gives the image a dreamy style with great visual impact.

name: Tiger
description: Lomography Tiger is Lomography's signature 110 mini-format color negative film, bringing vibrant color expression to the shooting experience that revives the era of compact pocket cameras. The film has a nominal ISO 200 sensitivity and can be processed through the standard C-41 color negative film processing process, making it compatible with most 110 models on the market. The image style of Tiger film tends to be bright colors and soft grain. It performs stably when there is sufficient light during the day, and can also be used with flash in low-light environments. Its default color saturation and contrast make the city street scenes, portraits and daily moments captured have a vivid and layered picture effect. Due to the size characteristics of the 110 negative itself, the grain becomes more obvious after enlargement, giving it a unique film texture.

name: Turquoise
description: Lomography LomoChrome Turquoise is an experimental and creative color negative film known for its unique turquoise color shift effect. The film uses an innovative emulsion formula that can be processed through the standard C-41 color negative film processing process, and has a wide sensitivity range of ISO 100-400, suitable for creative shooting in different lighting conditions. The biggest feature of Turquoise film is its color transformation ability: the original colors in daily scenes will be remapped into charming turquoise tones, while the sky, vegetation, buildings and other subjects may appear in colors such as sapphire blue, turquoise or dark cyan, forming a strong and surreal contrast with orange highlights and warm areas, giving the image a unique dreamy visual beauty.

100+ is Lucky's fine color negative film designed for daylight conditions. As the product of in-depth cooperation with Kodak, it has significantly improved the early color shift problem of domestic films while maintaining Lucky's consistently high cost performance. Its imaging style tends to be warm-toned, and its color reproduction under sunlight is very full, with a certain unique era texture. Although it is slightly less detailed than the Fuji Superia 100 of the same period, it has excellent saturation when expressing warm colors such as reds and yellows. It was the "first roll of film" for many Chinese photography enthusiasts. Its stable performance and affordable price made it the most authentic recorder of Chinese family images of that era.

Lucky 1021 is the "all-round cornerstone" of this series. Its sensitivity of around ISO 160 gives it excellent exposure adaptability and can capture large areas of the ground under conditions of varying atmospheric transparency. It is known for its high resolution and robust latitude. In the civilian field, it is the most easy-to-control aviation roll. After proper contrast reduction and processing, it can present delicate gray scales with a very steely texture. It is a common ration for photographers who pursue "large format details".

Lucky 1023 is an ISO 200 full-color black-and-white negative film that strikes an extremely delicate balance between light sensitivity and image detail. Compared with 1025, the emulsion layer of 1023 has higher photosensitivity efficiency and reduced contrast, maintaining the ultra-high line-pair resolution that is the hallmark of aerial film. In the civilian field, it is regarded as an excellent and low-price black and white film for beginners. Its solid graininess and strong light and shadow tension make it a sharp knife in the hands of street sweeps, documentaries, and photographers who pursue high-contrast film textures.

The Lucky 1025 is the most contrasting model in the range, with a sensitivity of ISO 64, making it a powerful tool for penetrating clouds and seeing through camouflage. 1025 has naturally high contrast and can easily tear through the cover of atmospheric fog. In the hands of photographers, its extremely high contrast can turn blue skies into late night, light up vegetation like snow, and produce dramatic and surreal black and white images. It is a representative of the most artistically charming aviation special photosensitive materials.

Lucky 200 is a domestic ISO 200 color negative film. The overall imaging orientation is natural and simple, the color saturation is moderate, slightly warm, and the skin color is life-like and realistic. The graininess is slightly more obvious than that of international brands of the same level, but the details and levels are still reliable in sunny environments. The tolerance is acceptable and suitable for daily street sweeping, documentary and retro-oriented creations, and the images have a distinct sense of age and local color style.

200+ is the "all-round universal" product in the Lucky series. It's designed to provide a wider shooting window, performing well both on cloudy days and in indoor light. The film has a livelier tonality than the 100-degree version, moderate contrast, and very good exposure latitude. Due to the use of improved color-forming agent technology, the skin color restored by 200+ is relatively natural without excessive grayness. It was China's "national ration roll" for street sweeping photography and travel photography at that time. Its imaging has a light, nostalgic film atmosphere, which can instantly give ordinary streets a visual look and feel with the warmth of life.

name: C1021
description: Lucky C1021 is the "all-round cornerstone" of the series. Lucky 1021 has a sensitivity of around ISO 160, which gives it excellent exposure adaptability and can capture large areas of the ground under conditions of changing atmospheric transparency. It is known for its high resolution and robust latitude. In the civilian field, it is the most easy-to-control aviation roll. After proper contrast reduction and processing, it can present delicate gray scales with a very steely texture. It is a common ration for photographers who pursue "large format details".

name: HD 400
description: Lucky HD 400 is a high-sensitivity full-color black and white negative film produced by the Chinese Lucky Company. It is a masterpiece in Lucky’s black and white product line that pursues a balance between high speed and high sharpness. As an ISO 400 black and white volume, HD 400 is known for its cool grayscale levels and strong tonal contrast, which can provide clear, sharp and three-dimensional images in low-light environments, indoor documentary or high-speed capture. After HD400, Lucky developed SHD400 film. It is one of the very few domestic black-and-white films that can take into account both "fast speed" and "fine image quality." It represents the height of Lucky's early research on black-and-white photosensitive emulsions.

name: II型 100
description: In 1986, Lucky 100 daylight color film (II) was officially put into industrial production, marking a breakthrough in domestic civilian color film and announcing the end of the era of black and white film in China. The ISO 100 sensitivity makes it stable in daylight conditions. Due to the limitations of emulsion technology at the time, Type 2 film is known for its rich warm red tones and grainy, nostalgic texture. It has moderate contrast and has an extremely keen ability to capture the red spectrum. This unique "Chinese red" expressiveness made it a collective visual memory for Chinese families of that era to record festivals, travels, and take photos in front of Tiananmen Square.

name: New SHD 100
description: Lucky New SHD100 is an ISO 100 black and white negative film re-produced by Lucky. It adopts a full-color emulsion design and supports standard black and white development processes. This film has a fine grain structure, balanced contrast and a wide exposure latitude, making the picture appear natural in the transition between light and dark, with clear details and rich gray scales. The New SHD100 can provide stable imaging under sufficient or moderate lighting conditions, with soft and layered textures, making it suitable for street photography, landscapes, portraits and daily creative photography. As a domestically produced product, it combines the texture of traditional black and white photography with modern practicality, making it a popular choice for entry-level and experimental photography.

name: New SHD 400
description: Lucky New SHD400 is the latest ISO 400 black and white negative film produced by Lucky. It is positioned as a high-sensitivity general-purpose black and white film and is suitable for shooting under various light conditions. Compared with the low-speed version, this film has more obvious grain and richer contrast. It performs better in low-light environments and has an expressive and textured image style. The New SHD400 can capture deep shadows and rich gray scales while maintaining good exposure latitude, allowing photographers to obtain controllable and textured results in street photography, documentary, night scenes and dynamic scenes. As part of Lucai's production resumption plan, it continues the brand's tradition in the field of black and white film and is suitable for creators who like high contrast and texture.

name: SHD 100
description: Lucky SHD 100 is a very representative domestic full-color black and white negative film. It has become the first choice for countless film photography enthusiasts because of its extremely high cost performance and unique imaging style. Its imaging style tends to be high-contrast and tough black-and-white transitions. Although the graininess is not delicate among ISO 100 films, this slightly rough texture actually enhances the intensity of documentary photography. Although the early SHD 100 posed certain scanning challenges due to its thin film base and easy curling after drying, its excellent development compatibility and extremely low cost of use make it still an irreplaceable creative tool in the hands of photographers who pursue a retro atmosphere and film texture.

name: SHD 100 专业型
description: Lucky SHD 100 Professional is actually a product of Lucky Company’s process improvement while retaining the original tone characteristics. In terms of photosensitive characteristics, the professional model still maintains the nominal sensitivity of ISO 100, and retains Lucky's signature high contrast, tough tones, and unique "holy light" highlight overflow effect when facing strong light sources. Its latitude has also been improved to a certain extent, allowing for a more solid performance of dark details. In general, the SHD 100 professional model has evolved from a simple "hand roll" to a creative black and white negative film with more reliable performance by improving physical stability and batch consistency while maintaining a very high cost performance.

name: SHD 400
description: Lucky SHD400 is a classic ISO 400 black and white negative film. It is famous for its high sensitivity, obvious grain and high contrast performance. It is sensitive to light and has a unique imaging style. Some photographers have found in real-life shots that it has a "cinematic" visual effect and deep black performance in strong shadows; some photography enthusiasts recommend exposing at ISO 200 in some cases to obtain a more ideal balance effect. While there have been mixed discussions about the quality and performance of past batches, it remains an experimental choice for many exploring black and white film expression styles.

name: 彩韵 200
description: Lucky Colorful 200 is a popular color negative film produced by China's Lucky Company. It was once one of the most competitive films in the Asian market. The ISO 200 sensitivity makes it a versatile choice for everyday recording, family gatherings and outdoor travel. Known for its bright, saturated colors and unique tendency toward warm red tones, this film excels at capturing the vivid atmosphere of sunlight. Although it is slightly inferior to the top professional rolls at the time in terms of grain fineness, Caiyun 200 has a simple and heavy narrative feel, and its color reproduction has a strong imprint of the times.

name: 超金 100
description: Lucky Super Gold 100 is a color negative film launched by China Lucky Company. Its ISO 100 sensitivity enables it to have extremely fine grain performance and excellent image sharpness in a well-lit environment. This film is known for its signature warm red tones and bright visual transparency, especially when capturing sun-kissed skin tones, red walls or natural scenery. It can present a rich, festive and vibrant tone. This unique color expression is affectionately known as "Lucky Red" by enthusiasts. Although it has bid farewell to the market with the discontinuation of the Lucky color production line, its stable tolerance and color tendency with oriental aesthetic characteristics have made it a classic benchmark for recording Chinese-style cultural landscapes and retro portraits.

name: 超金 200
description: Lucky Super Gold 200 is a versatile color negative film launched by the Chinese company Lucky at its peak. As the backbone of the "Super Gold" series, it achieves the perfect balance of fine grain and high sensitivity at a sensitivity of ISO 200. This film inherits the iconic warm red tone of the Lucky family, but compared to the 100-degree version, its tone is livelier and brighter, with excellent exposure latitude. Whether shooting outdoors on a bright day, on a cloudy afternoon, or shooting indoors with flash, the Super Gold 200 provides extremely stable imaging performance. It restores skin color with a natural rosiness, high color saturation and sharp contrast. It was the film of choice for countless photographers at that time to record weddings, folklore and social documentaries. Although it has been discontinued, its "golden tone" with oriental charm is still an insurmountable classic in the history of domestic color film.

name: Color QRS 100
description: ORWO Color QRS 100 is a professional-grade color negative film launched by the Wolfen factory in Germany in the 1990s. As the ORWO brand's modern foray into color photography, a sensitivity of ISO 100 gives it fine grain and extreme sharpness in daylight. Unlike Western films of the same period, QRS 100 continued the rigorous and slightly cold color style of the East German industry. It has moderate saturation and restores skin tones with a natural flesh-pink feel rather than excessive warmth. Its dark performance is solid, showing a unique "European cool tone" and deep contrast. Although it disappeared into the long history with the turmoil of the original ORWO factory, QRS 100 is still regarded by film collectors as a precious sample to study the "low contrast, high detail" aesthetics of German negatives.

name: DN 21
description: Wolfen DN21 is a black-and-white negative film from Germany's ORWO traditional film system. It was originally used as an intermediate negative for film production, but its unique image characteristics are also very suitable for still photography. This film is a full-color black-and-white film with a very low nominal sensitivity of ISO 8, which is suitable for shooting scenes with sufficient light or where very delicate levels are required. DN21 has extremely low graininess and excellent resolution. It can display balanced mid-tones and deep and full blacks. The grayscale transition of the picture is soft and natural. It is suitable for creative photography of portraits, landscapes and high-detail expressions. An anti-vignetting layer is added to the film to help reduce halos under backlighting and improve image clarity and contrast. As an "industrial-grade" black-and-white film with both a sense of history and technology, DN21 is not only an interesting choice for experimental images, but also provides unique style expression possibilities for photographers who like ultra-detailed, richly layered black-and-white images.

name: NC 400
description: Wolfen NC400 is an ISO400 color negative film launched by the German ORWO brand. It adopts the standard C-41 process and can be processed in the conventional color negative film process. The film was re-developed based on the chemical formula of traditional Agfa negatives and presents a unique color style: the tone is cooler and more green-leaning, the shadows are desaturated and the fine graininess is restrained. NC400 has good imaging stability and natural gradation in a well-lit environment, with moderate color saturation. It is suitable for street photography, portraits, travel and daily creation, and brings a visual experience to photographic images that is different from mainstream consumer-grade negative films.

name: NC 500
description: Woflen NC500 is another ISO400 color negative film launched by the ORWO brand that also supports standard C-41 processing. It is based on the improved formula of the legendary Agfa XT320 film film emulsion, emphasizing softer colors and hazy atmosphere, with warmer tones, slightly desaturated colors in shadows, and a more obvious and well-structured grain texture. The color performance of NC500 is different from traditional consumer-grade films, presenting a unique green rich tone and film-like texture, which is suitable for photographers who pursue a different color style.

name: P400
description: Wolfen P400 is a high-sensitivity black-and-white film from the German ORWO brand, which continues the image characteristics of ORWO's traditional film emulsions. The film has a nominal sensitivity of ISO 400, which is suitable for shooting in low light or dynamic scenes, with good exposure latitude and stable performance. ORWO P400 has a balanced contrast and textured grain structure, rich grayscale levels, solid light and dark details, and can present classic black and white image styles under various lighting conditions. Although the graininess of the film is slightly obvious, its structure is compact and full of expressive power of traditional film. It is very suitable for street photography, documentary, portrait and daily creative photography. As a member of the ORWO series of black and white films, P400 continues the robust characteristics of German film manufacturing.
